title.en: Before His Father Finished Speaking, the Heir Accused the Trustee
title.zh: 父亲仍在致辞，继承人却当众剑指家族受托人

description.en: One sealed envelope, one disputed signature and two hundred witnesses turn an elegant engagement gala into a fight over who has been controlling the…
description.zh: 一个封口信封、一处存疑签名和两百名宾客，让华丽订婚晚宴变成了一场关于谁在暗中控制整个家族的较量。

title.en: Before His Father Finished Speaking, the Heir Accused the Trustee
title.zh: 父亲话音未落，继承人便剑指受托人

summary.en: At a rooftop engagement gala, Adrian publicly accuses the family's longtime trustee of swapping a signed succession agreement. The sealed documents soon expose forged pages, hidden triggers and a system built to decide his future without him.
summary.zh: 在一场露台订婚晚宴上，Adrian 当众指控家族受托人偷换已签署的继承协议。封存文件随即牵出伪造页面、隐藏触发条款，以及一个长期背着他决定其未来的权力体系。

warning.en: Fiction. Contains intense family conflict, legal and financial manipulation, forged documents, police questioning, emotional distress and minor injury.
warning.zh: 虚构故事。包含激烈家庭冲突、法律与财务操控、文件伪造、警方问询、情绪崩溃及轻微受伤情节。

en: ## Chapter One
The sudden silence allowed Adrian to hear his own breathing clearly. He could feel the dry pull in the back of his throat, and to his chagrin, Helena was obviously aware of his tightness.
“I was going to the morning room to get Celia’s shawl,” he broke the silence. “The patio door was open and Helena was standing in front of the display table.”
“I’m just checking the documents.” Helena’s expression remained unchanged.
Charles didn’t look at her. “Let him finish.”

Adrian stared at her and continued, “She had two envelopes in her hands. One was the official one and the other was her own. I saw her pull out the signed agreement from the envelope Margot had left on the table and stuff the other document inside. She then sealed the second envelope and took it out.”
Helena tilted her head slightly. “All you see is paper.”
“I saw the signature page.”
“From a distance of fifteen feet, you just saw something that 'looked like' a signature page.”
“I saw my father’s initials in blue ink.”

Charles' eyes fell on the envelope on his desk. That afternoon he had signed every page of the inheritance agreement. Adrian was sure of this, for his father had complained bitterly about the pen Helena had forced him to use.
Celia stood so close that her bare arms almost touched Adrian’s sleeves. “Then why didn’t you point it out right away?”
Adrian glanced at her. The question was sharp, but it really hit home.
“I followed Helena out,” he confessed. “I wanted to make sure. She walked into the hallway to the bathroom and came back with only an envelope in her hand. Then my dad started to give his speech.”
“So you endured the six-minute speech before you had an attack.” There was no emotion in Charles' tone.
“Because I thought maybe I was wrong.”
Helena let out a very soft sigh. “You did see it wrong.”
Adrian turned to her sharply: “Then it was outside just now, why did you stop everyone from opening it?”
“Because it would be an irreversible disaster to disgrace this family in front of two hundred guests.”
“The civet cat exchanges for the prince, and the secret exchange of legal documents is also an irreversible disaster!”
“Adrian,” Charles warned in a deep voice.
The warning tone was all too familiar. Its subtext is: Don’t make me deal with you first while I deal with the really important things. Adrian shut his mouth.
Charles turned to Helena. “What’s in the envelope?”
“A revised executive copy.”
“Who revised it?”
“Me.”
“Who gave you the authorization?”
Helena’s mouth tightened. “You.”
Charles stared at her.
“No, I didn’t,” he said every word.
Helena glanced at the closed door, as if to confirm the absolute privacy of the room. “It was you who asked me to modify the terms of the survivor settings.”
“I’m asking you to prepare a few 'alternative plans'.”
“Your original statement was that the existing structure would put the estate at risk.”
“I also said that we will discuss this matter on Monday.”
“You also said that once the news of the engagement is announced, any delay would be unwise.”
“But I never authorized you to make a 'replacement'.”
The word “replacement” changes the air density in the room.
This is not a misunderstanding. It’s not an administrative error. It was not a nervous young man who misjudged the routine of a senior consultant.
Celia stepped away from Adrian and looked directly at Helena. “What exactly did you change?”
Helena looked back at her with an irritating coolness. “This has nothing to do with you at the moment.”
“If my engagement is a reason for you to tamper with documents, that concerns me.”
“It’s about your future, so it needs to be discussed with extreme caution.”
Charles reached out for the envelope. Just a moment before he touched her, Helena moved. The movement is not big, just half a step. But enough is enough. Charles' hand hovered in the air.
“What did you put in there?” he asked sharply.
Helena’s expression regained some of its usual dignity. “A document that protects an estate from unwanted transfer of assets.”
“Transferred to whom?”
No one answered. Adrian felt Celia stiffen beside him.
Charles lowered his gaze and studied the seal. He turned the envelope over and examined the raised crown relief. “This is not our family’s fire seal.”
“No,” Helena admitted.
“Whose is that?”
“Mine.”

Charles looked up. For years, Helena had used the family crest of Ward Trust Partners on her personal letterhead, even though that firm had long since been absorbed into a larger trust. The crown and laurels once belonged to her grandfather, a probate judge in New Haven, and his portrait still hangs in a courthouse conference room.
Charles pinched the envelope.
“We’ll take it apart now.”
A crack finally cracks in Helena’s disguise, revealing the underlying fear.
“If you take it apart without an attorney present, it could significantly damage your position.”
“What position?”
“A position in a legal dispute that you’re not even aware of yet.”

Charles broke the seal without hesitation. The voice is very soft. Adrian expected to see something dramatic—a hidden amendment, a forged conveyance, or ruthless terms that would see him out. Instead, Charles simply pulled out a twelve-page document pinned to the top with a paper clip and read the title page with a blank expression.
Celia moved closer. Adrian couldn’t read the words clearly. Charles turned to page two. Then the third page.
“What on earth is that?” Adrian couldn’t help but ask.
Charles turned a deaf ear. Helena closed her eyes in pain.
Charles finally looked up at her. “You transferred voting control of Vale Shipping Holdings to the trust.”
“I’m here to preserve it.”
“You put my controlling shares into an irrevocable management structure.”
“The trust originally held a residual interest.”
“That was after I died!”
“Your recent series of decisions have created an imminent crisis.”
“You mean my decision to approve Adrian’s marital property agreement?”
“I’m referring to your decision to tie the entire estate to the potential debt of the Markham family.”
The color drained from Celia’s face. “My family has nothing against Vale shipping!”
“There is indeed none today,” Helena said tit-for-tat, “But that is different from 'no risk exposure'.”
Charles slammed the papers onto the table. “This has my signature on it.”
Adrian leaned forward sharply. At the bottom of the page, Charles' name appears in a firm line of blue ink. Charles tapped the signature lightly with his index finger.
“I never signed this document.”

The whole audience could hear the needle drop. He turned to another page. The blue initials stand out, with a familiar tilt. Familiar enough to silence any doubts. Celia looked at Adrian. Before she spoke, he had read the question in her eyes.
“You said you saw her replace the signed agreement,” she asked shakily, “Did you see her sign anything?”
“No.”
“Did anyone see that?”
Helena’s eyes drifted to him. Adrian hated the look of relief in her eyes. Charles picked up his phone and dialed a number.
“Daniel,” he ordered as soon as the call came through, “come to the library right now. Now.”

He hung up without waiting for the other party to respond. Daniel Price, Charles' personal lawyer, also attended the dinner tonight with his husband, and is probably still pretending to study a dessert plate on the terrace. Less than two minutes later, he pushed open the door and walked in. As soon as he saw the documents on the table, he immediately closed the door and loosened his tie.
## Chapter Two
“I heard something was wrong,” Daniel said.
“A transfer of control document with a forged signature.” Charles responded coldly.
Daniel’s eyes suddenly became sharp. “Everybody don’t touch anything.”
“I’ve already taken it apart.”
“That’s such a shame.”
“It was in Helena’s possession.”
“That would be even more regrettable.”
Helena turned to him: “Before anyone uses the word 'forgery' again, you’d better check this executive copy with the set of signed documents this afternoon.”
Daniel walked over to his desk but didn’t touch the papers. “Where are the signed documents for this afternoon?”
“In the official envelope on the display table in the morning lounge,” Adrian answered.
Daniel immediately looked at Charles. “Send someone to block it.”
“Margot’s right outside the door.”
“At least sixty people came in and out of that room tonight.”
“Two hundred,” Celia corrected.
Daniel pulled out his phone. “I asked security to lock the south door.”
Helena folded her hands. “You are creating a farce that will never end.”
“The farce begins the moment you step onto the stage of a public ceremony holding a document with an unauthorized signature,” Charles retorted.
She looked at him with an almost sad look. “You are still deceiving yourself into thinking that the signature is 'unauthorized'.”
Adrian stared hard at his father’s face. Charles didn’t flinch, but there was an indescribable fluctuation in the depths of his eyes.
“What does that mean?” Daniel asked.
Helena remained silent.
Daniel turned to Charles. “Have you signed any backup drafts today?”
“No.”
“What about yesterday?”
“No.”
“This week?”
“No.”
“Have you ever signed a blank signature page?”
Charles' silence lasted too long. Adrian turned sharply to look at his father.
Daniel’s tone changed: “Charles.”
“I signed a confirmation of a batch of restructuring documents on Tuesday.”
“How many servings?”
“I don’t know. Fifteen? Or twenty.”
“Are they stapled together?”
“They were presented to me as a complete set of closing documents.”
“Who submitted it?”
Charles looked at Helena. She returned his gaze without giving in.
Daniel rubbed his brow painfully. “You actually signed that pile of documents without reviewing the attachments one by one?”
“I reviewed the abstract.”
“A summary prepared by Helena?”
“Yes.”
Adrian couldn’t help but take a step back, away from the desk.

The air in the library seems to be getting a little hot. The collar of his shirt was suffocating him. For most of his life, he had thought that his father was outrageously cautious. Charles would double-check restaurant bills, record backups after board meetings, and never even sign a birthday card message without personally checking it. However, he actually signed a whole pile of documents without hesitation just because Helena handed them over - just because Helena had been doing this every day for the past twenty-three years.
Celia lowered her voice and said, “So, the signature may be genuine.”

“The document may not have been attached at all when it was signed,” Daniel analyzed, “or it may have been disguised as something else and mixed in the package. These are two completely different types of trouble.”
Helena’s hands were still folded. “This document is in Tuesday’s packet.”
Charles glared at her: “Nonsense.”
“It is listed as a ‘contingent governance instrument’.”
“It was marked 'Draft' at the time!”
“The catalog doesn’t say 'draft.'”
“But it’s in the abstract!”
“The summary clearly states that the document’s effectiveness is dependent on a triggering event.”
“What’s the triggering event?”
Helena’s eyes flickered between Adrian and Celia.
“Public engagement.”
For several seconds, no one spoke.
Celia laughed suddenly, without any trace of laughter. “My engagement triggered the transfer of control of his company?”
“It’s not just the engagement,” Helena explained, “it’s the public announcement of the engagement, coupled with that revised marital estate proposal submitted by your family’s attorney.”
“My family’s attorneys only sent a draft.”
“A draft requesting an ‘equal share’ of future asset appreciation.”
“That simply refers to the assets between Adrian and me.”
“Unless the existing shareholding structure is changed, Adrian’s future asset appreciation cannot be separated from the trust fund’s holdings.”
Adrian looked at Celia in disbelief. “You never told me that.”
“I had no idea there was such a clause in it.”
“That’s what your lawyer wrote.”
“That was from 'my father’s' lawyer!”
“But you signed it?”
“I just told them to draw up a standard agreement.”
Helena’s expression softened slightly. “When it comes to family succession control, there is no 'standard protocol' in this world.”
Charles picked up the transfer document. “So your brilliant solution is to take away my voting rights before the engagement becomes public?”
“My solution is to prevent a mired marital claim from paralyzing the entire company.”
“That’s 'my' company.”
“That’s 'your family’s' company.”
Charles stared hard at her.

Daniel forced himself between the table and the fireplace, putting his body in the middle of the conflict. “Tonight we will not address the issue of interpretation of the terms. The priority now is to seal all documents, confirm every version, lock down everyone’s access and absolutely not continue the argument in front of unnecessary witnesses.”
“I’m not an unnecessary witness,” Adrian retorted.
Daniel looked at him. “Not only are you a witness, but that means you must now keep your mouth shut until I get your exact confession in writing.”
Adrian once again felt the long-lost humiliation of being reduced to a role at the mercy of others.
“I know exactly what I just saw.”
“I believe you did see 'something'. But I need to know the precise details now, and that’s before your memory is reshaped by the next ten conversations.”
Helena turned to Charles. “You should also be aware that this transfer document has been set and will be delivered to the Trust’s administrative offices at nine o’clock tomorrow morning.”
“You arranged the delivery schedule.” Daniel exposed her.
“Yes.”
“Can you cancel?”
“Yes.”
“Cancel immediately.”
Helena remained motionless.
Daniel’s voice suddenly dropped to freezing point. “Right now.”
“This phone doesn’t work.”
“Then call someone who can handle it.”
“Directions are controlled by external fiduciary advisers.”
“Name.”
“Becker Lane Law Firm.”
Daniel gasped. “It’s indeed them.”
Charles frowned: “What do you mean?”
“Meaning, they represent the trust, not you. If the document is legal, their role may be to force the transfer; if it is illegal, they will remain on hold until they know how much risk they face.”
Charles walked over to the bar cart and poured some water into the crystal glasses. It wasn’t until he picked up the cup that his hands began to tremble. Adrian saw it. Helena saw it too.
Charles swallowed, put down his glass, and looked at his son.
“You’re right to speak out.”
This statement should have brought some kind of redemptive relief, but instead, it only made Adrian feel incredibly immature.
“You believe me?” he asked.
“I believe Helena moved the documents without authorization.”
“That’s not what I asked.”
Charles' expression closed slightly. “We still don’t know exactly what happened.”

Adrian looked away. Celia tried to get closer to him, but he took a step back before she could touch him. Daniel was now giving instructions to security personnel to seal all access logs in the morning lounge, south hallway, library, and west service entrance. He asked for photos of the display table to be taken and ordered that no staff member leave their post without leaving their contact information.
## Chapter Three
Helena stared at him, her expression almost calm. Adrian was the first to notice the change.
“You’re not scared now,” he said.
She turned her head. “Panic is useless.”
“You were clearly panicking outside just now.”
“Because a young man who knew nothing about the cause and effect accused me of fraud in public.”
“You did slip the envelope.”
“Yes.”
This straightforward admission caused the whole room to fall into another strange silence.
Adrian took a step closer to her. “Then why are you still pretending-”
“I switched the package because the document that was originally scheduled to be displayed was not the one that your father really wanted to make public.”
Charles put down the crystal glass in his hand. “Speak clearly.”
Helena looked at the opened envelope. “In the inheritance agreement on the display table, the control transfer document was quietly inserted as an attachment.”
Daniel froze. “You mean the official inheritance agreement?”
“Yes.”
“Who put it in?”
“I don’t know.”
Charles narrowed his eyes. “You expect us to believe that you took one unauthorized document and then put in another unauthorized document just for 'protection'?”

“I replaced the public executive copy with the governance document that was signed on Tuesday because I had to remove the tampered package without alerting the person who had tampered with the document.”
“This is absolutely ridiculous,” Celia interjected.
“If Helena thought someone was spying on that table at that time, the logic would be valid,” Daniel said quietly.
Adrian looked at him in shock. “You’re actually defending her?”
“I’m just clarifying the logic, it doesn’t mean I agree with her approach.”
Charles turned to Helena. “Why don’t you just hand me that packet?”
“Because I’m not sure whether you acquiesced in stuffing it in.”
“You can ask me.”
“In front of all the guests? Minutes before your speech?”
“You can take me aside and talk in private.”
“You were chatting with the lieutenant governor, then Celia’s parents, then the photographer. I had to make a snap decision.”
“An reckless decision.”
“Yes.”
She answered so frankly that Charles was speechless for a moment.

Helena continued: “I originally planned to show the tampered agreement to Daniel after the speech. I used my own envelope because I could not reseal the official envelope. I specifically chose a document that would trigger an internal review if discovered.”
Adrian stared at her in astonishment. “Did you mean to get caught?”
“I hope this unreasonableness can be noticed by a knowledgeable person.”
“You looked horrified when Margot noticed the paint marks.”
“Because Margot shouted it to the whole terrace.”
“These are completely different things,” Daniel interrupted. “Why on earth did you have to put the signed transfer documents in your envelope?”
“To keep the weight and thickness of the envelope consistent.”
Daniel’s expression changed again. “So, anyone watching from a distance will mistakenly think that the original display document is still in place.”
“Yes.”
Charles said solemnly: “You mean there are accomplices in this room.”
“I mean, the agreement on the table was tampered with before I even touched it.”
Adrian shook his head desperately. “I saw you pull out the paper with my own eyes.”
“What you saw was me taking the tampered packet.”
“Then it was replaced.”
“Yes.”
“With a document bearing his signature.”
“Yes.”
“Without informing him at all.”
“Yes.”
Every admission compresses the living space around her a little bit. But Helena didn’t flinch a step.
Daniel pulled out a clean white paper from the table and carefully placed the unpacked transfer document into a leather briefcase. “We need to find the official envelope.”

There was a knock on the door. Margot pushed the door open without waiting for a response from inside. Her invisible earphones were gone, and a strand of blond hair fell out of her ponytail and clung to her sweaty cheeks.
“The display envelope is missing,” she reported.
Tonight, for the first time, Charles finally completely lost expression control.
“What did you say?”
“I locked the morning room as I was told. When the guests were invited inside for dessert, the envelope was still on the table. But when security closed the south door, it was gone.”
Daniel looked sharply at Helena. She didn’t move at all. Adrian felt Celia turn around him.
Margot took a breath and continued: “The pen is still there. The silver tray is too. Only the envelope is gone.”
“Who has been in during this time?” Daniel asked.
“There was probably a three-minute window where everyone on the terrace could have gotten in.”
“Where’s the surveillance?”
“Mr. Vale requested that the patio cameras be turned off to protect his privacy.”
Charles cast his gaze to the ground. Two years ago, a private photo of him at a retirement dinner hit the gossip columns, and he’s had this rule ever since.
“What about indoor surveillance?” Daniel asked.
“Only in the hallway. Not in the morning lounge.”
“Is there an entrance or exit?”
“Yes.”
“Seal the manor immediately.”
Charles raised his head sharply: “No.”
Daniel turned to face him: “A legal document that was most likely tampered with has just been stolen.”
“You cannot illegally detain two hundred guests who are either rich or distinguished.”
“I can ask them to help investigate a security incident and stay on hold for now.”
“This will put this scandal in the news headlines before midnight.”
“It might have been in the news.”
As if to confirm this statement, Celia’s phone vibrated. Next up is Adrian’s. And then there’s Charles’s.
Celia was the first to see the screen clearly. “Someone posted the video online.”

Adrian pulled out his phone. This video was uploaded less than a minute ago by a completely unfamiliar account. In the picture, he was pale and pointing furiously across the terrace, and the voice-over was his own roar: She secretly changed the agreement!

The video ends abruptly before Margot can speak. The eye-catching title reads: [Shocking Scandal at Engagement Dinner: Vale Family Heir Publicly Accuses Family Trustee of Fraud] Adrian forced himself to read it twice. When he watched it for the second time, he was shocked to realize how hysterical he looked in the video.

That’s not perseverance, let alone courage. It was out-of-control madness. Another tweet popped up right below, from a local political reporter—who only got the invitation because Charles sponsors half the charities in the state.
Sources say the dispute centers on control of Vale Shipping and a draft matrimonial property agreement. Celia flipped her phone back onto the table.
“My parents will definitely think I orchestrated all this.”
Adrian looked at her in shock. “Why do they think that?”
“Because Helena just accused my family’s lawyer of causing hidden dangers, and now, a top-secret private agreement has become a public gossip on the Internet before the dessert is even served.”
“I’m not accusing your family.”
“But you accused the family trustee in front of everyone.”
“Because I saw with my own eyes that she dropped the documents!”
“And now, the only document that explains why she did what she did is missing.”

There was no blame in her words, but that was all the more despairing. Charles looked past them to the closed door of the library. The guests outside the door are no longer guests, but an uncontrollable torrent. They must be frantically scrolling through their cell phones, calling drivers, and making up various versions of conspiracy theories.
“Margot,” he finally gave in, “please everyone stay for fifteen more minutes. Just say that an important document is missing from the manor and we need their assistance.”
## Chapter Four
“Assist?” Daniel raised his eyebrows.
“We can’t search the senator.”
“We may have to search the staff.”
“No.”
“The envelope really flew away.”
“It could have flown away.”
Daniel stared at him: “Your instinct to always put 'face' first is the reason why there isn’t even a surveillance camera in that room!”
Charles gritted his teeth: “Watch your words.”
“No, not tonight.”
Their decades-long friendship allowed this level of offense, and the cracks in this friendship were unreservedly exposed in front of everyone.
Margot was still standing by the door. “One more question.”
No one answered.
“The envelope used for the official display had black paint on the seal,” she said, “not red.”
Adrian looked sharply at her.
Helena responded: “What I saw was black too.”
“But when ordering stationery the request was for dark navy.”
Charles frowned: “What?”

Margot walks into the room. “These envelopes arrived this morning. Twelve rigid gold-foil envelopes in total, all stamped with the Vale family compass rose in dark navy. At five-forty, I put one of them on the table. But when I checked again at six-ten, the stamp was black.”
“You just left it there?” Daniel asked sharply.
“I thought it was a lighting problem, making the dark blue look darker.”
“Who else knows the details of the paint color?”
“The stationer. My team. Mrs. Kline, housekeeper. Mr. Vale’s administrative assistant. And Helena.”
Helena shook her head. “I’ve only seen the design drawings and don’t know the final color.”
Margot turned to Adrian. “What color was the paint on the envelope you saw she took?”
“Black.”
“What about the one she left behind?”
“Red.”
“So the envelope covered in black paint had been tampered with before Helena touched it.”
Celia stared at Adrian: “Then from beginning to end, have you ever seen the official envelope printed with 'dark navy blue' paint?”

He tried his best to reconstruct the scene in his mind. The open door to the morning lounge. A shawl draped over the back of a chair. Helena standing in front of the glass table. Gold foil envelopes in left and right hands. Black fire paint. Red fire paint. His father’s blue initials. The slight sound of paper rubbing against each other.
“No,” he replied sullenly.
Helena’s shoulders relaxed slightly. Even though this new clue cleared Helena of some of her suspicions, Adrian still felt a twinge of annoyance at the relief on her face.
Charles looked at Margot. “Go find the other eleven envelopes.”
“They’re in a locked storage room.”
“Go check it out.”
Margot takes the order and leaves.

Daniel placed his hands on the table. “We are now faced with three thorny questions. First: Did Charles knowingly sign the transfer document? Second: Who stuffed the tampered agreement into the black envelope. Third: Who stole the envelope from the table after the accusation just now.”
“And a fourth one,” Celia added, “who posted the video online before anyone even left the terrace.”
Daniel glanced at her. “Yes.”

Adrian stared at his phone screen. The original post has been wildly forwarded by the big V account. The comment area below is full of netizens who didn’t know who he was yesterday, but tonight they have become micro-expression experts and psychology masters.

The privileged rich second generation suffers a nervous breakdown at their engagement party. The little prince of the trust fund woke up and found that his family property was about to be lost. Why doesn’t this woman run away quickly?
He turned off the screen. Helena was watching him.
“This is the situation I tried my best to avoid,” she said.
Adrian met her gaze. “And you were holding a top-secret asset transfer document in your hands at the time.”
“So you exposed it completely before even understanding what it was.”
“You could have stopped and explained it.”
“If I explain, will you listen?”
He opened his mouth, but nothing came out.
Celia crossed her arms. “I really want to know why this control transfer document is related to our engagement in the first place?”
Charles motioned to Daniel: “Now is not the time to discuss this.”
“Now!” She raised her voice. “My name has been dragged into this quagmire.”
“Your name is not on the transfer document.”
“But my family is being guarded against as some kind of debt hazard!”
“That’s Helena’s fault.”
“But her excuse was a draft sent by our family’s lawyer.”
Charles' silence drove Celia mad more than any denial.
She took a deep breath and turned to Adrian. “Have you read the marital property draft carefully?”
He looked at her guiltily.

They had been trying to negotiate this agreement for three weeks. While lawyers on both sides bickered over the terms, the couple argued over the date of the wedding, the guest list, and whether to renovate the harborside cottage or move to Manhattan after the wedding. Every time the agreement came up, Celia would push it to her father’s lawyer; every time Adrian’s lawyer called, he would let his voicemail collect dust until the next day.
“I read the abstract,” he answered bravely.
A bitter curve formed at the corner of her mouth. “Of course you only read the summary.”

Charles cast complicated eyes on his son. The striking resemblance between father and son then seemed so ironic. Adrian realizes this too. Daniel’s cell phone rang. He glanced at the screen and answered the call.
“I’m Price.”
He listened to the report on the other end.
“When did it happen?”
His eyes raked over Helena like razor blades.
“Send me the records.”
He hangs up.
“What’s wrong?” Charles asked.
“Becker Lane Law Firm received an electronic transfer notice at 6:32 tonight.”
Helena glanced at the clock on the mantelpiece. The public accusation on the terrace took place at 7:18.
Daniel continued: “A scanned copy of the signed governance instrument was attached to the notice and instructions were given that the original would be delivered tomorrow.”
“Who sent it?” Charles' voice was as cold as ice.
“The sender is using encryption credentials from the Helena company.”
Everyone’s eyes were piercing her. Helena made no excuses.
Daniel spread his hands. “Cell phone.”
She stared at him.
“Now, right away.”
Helena took out a slim black mobile phone from her dinner bag and placed it on her desk.
“Password.”
“No.”
Charles whispered her name, with warning.
“My phone was filled with records of privileged communications involving other clients.”
Daniel let out a cold sneer. “Are you talking to me about confidentiality now?”
“I’m trying to avoid further breaches of professional ethics because everyone in this room is already in disarray!”
“Your credentials sent a highly controversial transfer of control document!”
“That doesn’t mean I sent it!”
“Then unlock your phone!”
“I will turn it over to independent third-party counsel for review.”
“You have to give it to me!”
“You don’t represent Charles.”
Daniel bolted upright. “For twenty years, you have always regarded yourself as his only spokesperson as long as you thought it was beneficial to you!”
Helena’s face turned pale. “And you’ve been racking up exorbitant bills for twenty years by giving him advice that he doesn’t even listen to!”
Charles, with the weariness of old age, forced himself between them. At that moment, he looked far older than fifty-two. “Shut up, everyone.”

There was a second knock on the door. Margot walked in holding a white storage cardboard box. She placed the box on the side table and lifted the lid. Neatly stacked inside were eleven gold-foil envelopes, each sealed in dark navy lacquer emblazoned with the Vale family compass rose.
“All the extra ones are here, not a few,” she said, “But, I found this under the moisture-proof oil paper.”
She picked up a slender piece of black paint. Daniel quickly snapped a photo before Margot put it down.
“Did it fall from some seal?” he asked.
## Chapter Five
“It’s the residue that fell off the edge of the seal, with a trace of gold foil fiber stuck to it,” Margot answered.
“This means that someone opened one of the dark navy envelopes and resealed it with black paint,” Celia pointed out astutely.
Margot nodded.

“In order to be able to refute you with reason when I quarrel with you.”

Charles gave a rare laugh. This was the first time in months that father and son had such unburdened laughter. Adrian enrolled in Columbia University’s advanced course in shipping finance and accepted a position as a rotating observer at Vale Shipping. The position comes with no voting rights and no guarantee of advancement — it’s a special committee proposal, not a handout from Charles.
On his first day at work, an employee in the elevator recognized him as the “crazy young man” who accused the trustee in public in the video, and immediately lowered his head in fear.
Another employee whispered behind him: “Look, 'Brother Agreement' is here.”

Adrian heard it clearly. But he still walked to his desk expressionlessly. Celia moves out of her parents' stifling mansion. She rented a modest apartment in Greenwich. She picked every piece of furniture inside, and there was a broken drawer in the kitchen that couldn’t be closed. Adrian had gone to great lengths to help her fix it once. Two days later it got stuck again. She simply left it open.

They first received long-term psychological counseling separately, and then began to try couples counseling together. The atmosphere of the first joint consultation was awkward and full of utilitarianism. They discuss the bottom line of financial disclosure, the boundaries of family of origin, and whether anyone really wants to hold a large and expensive wedding like a negotiation.

Celia admits that now she doesn’t even know if she still wants to get married. Adrian admitted that he still longed for this marriage in his heart, but before, he had always used the tedious wedding preparations as an excellent excuse to avoid facing the nature of marriage.
The psychotherapist pointedly asked what marriage meant to him.
He talked endlessly for three minutes, and suddenly discovered to his horror that all the words he just described pointed to “defense and protection” rather than “fighting side by side.”
Celia breaks down and cries. Adrian made no attempt to hug her or offer any words of comfort. He just spread his hands on his knees and sat quietly, waiting patiently for her.

Three months after the disastrous dinner, Thomas reached a plea deal with prosecutors in court, pleading guilty to two counts of obstruction of justice and unlawful conspiracy in exchange for prosecutors dropping the most damning conspiracy charge. He was sentenced to probation, paid an astronomical fine, and was permanently removed from the boards of several public companies.
## Chapter Sixteen

Celia attended the sentencing alone. Adrian avoided it. In the noisy corridor of the court, Thomas apologized tearfully to his daughter and tried to defend himself, saying that everything he did was to ensure her future happiness.
Celia looked at him coldly: “But that’s not love.”
Thomas' face was covered in wounds as if he had been hit by bullets. She took a deep breath and corrected herself.
“In other words, it’s not just love.”
Still, she stepped forward and hugged him tightly.

Owen rejected any form of plea deal and vowed to fight to the death in court. His legal team portrayed him as a righteous whistleblower, a hero who sacrificed himself to expose the abuse of power by greedy trustees. The prosecutors ruthlessly tore off his disguise and reduced him to an ambitious and unscrupulous careerist - he deliberately created a crisis, forcibly activated the controversial transfer agreement, spent money to fan the flames in the media, and tried to profit from this power vacuum of control.

To be fair, both versions are mixed with disgusting truths. Helena surprisingly agrees to testify. A few days before the trial, she asked Adrian to meet him at a seedy cafe near the New Haven courthouse. Her signature, meticulously high bun was gone. Her dark brown hair hangs casually on her shoulders, and a few dazzling gray strands can be clearly seen on the temples.
Gone are the pearls, diamonds and the oppressive black business attire. She no longer looks like an invincible queen, but has a touch of strange mortal air.
“It was you who asked to see me.” Adrian sat down opposite her.
“Yes.”
She pushed a thick folder across the table. It was filled with copies of every top-secret evaluation memo she had written about him for the trust since he turned eighteen and came of age.
He frowned at her. “Why should I look at this garbage?”
“You at least have the right to know how judgments are made on your behalf in those rooms where you are absent.”
He opened the first copy casually.

The phrasing is still that stifling clinical pathology style. “When faced with the trustee education that must be fulfilled, Adrian showed an obvious tendency to evade. The so-called media entrepreneurial plan he submitted completely lacked the most basic financial budget discipline. Adrian is vulnerable to severe financial influence from external forces in an intimate partnership.”
He closed the folder with a snap.
“I hate you so much,” he said through gritted teeth.
Helena nodded slightly. Her attitude of not even bothering to say a word of defense made his anger explode.
“Don’t sit there and act like a holy mother who just accepts everything! As if this can make up for all the sins you’ve committed!”
“It doesn’t make up for it.”
“Every word in these official documents you imply is that I am an inferior asset with factory defects!”
“Yes.”
“You watched me grow up!”
“Yes.”
“You clearly know why I desperately want to escape from that damn company!”
“I thought I knew.”
“You also clearly know how much I hate being like a puppet on strings, being manipulated at will in those rooms where I can’t even enter the door!”
“Yes.”
“But you did it in cold blood.”
“Yes.”
He pushed the folder hard back in front of her. Helena didn’t put it away.
“I wrote a separate statement,” she said.
“I don’t want to see any bullshit statement you write to the court.”
“This is not for the courts.”
“Then I don’t want to see it anymore.”

She lowered her gaze and stared at the cold coffee in front of her. The door of the cafe was pushed open, and a biting cold wind blew in. A student sitting by the window quickly put his hand down on the paper that was being blown.

Helena said quietly: “Throughout my career, I have always believed in an unshakable truth: The most stupid mistake a person can make is to fail to take decisive action before the danger really surfaces.”
Adrian stared at her and didn’t answer.

“Because of his luck, my father watched helplessly as his partners embezzled public funds until countless clients went bankrupt and ended up with his entire law firm. Your grandfather also kept delaying the transfer of power until a stroke completely incapacitated him, leaving everyone in the family Every decision has become a piece of cake on the chopping block. Your mother’s condition has irreversibly worsened as the family chose to delay time and time again in order to maintain superficial peace. I have engraved the idea of “eliminating hidden dangers in advance” into my bones and become the only value of my existence.”
“You just use it as an excuse for you to enjoy being absolutely needed.”
“Yes.”
He looked at her coldly.

She continued: “I didn’t even realize when this so-called 'anticipation' mutated into a pathological desire for absolute control. Or maybe I had already noticed it, but I regarded it with peace of mind as the price I had to pay to maintain efficient operation.”
“This line sounds like it was rehearsed countless times in front of the mirror.”
“Indeed. I’ve recited it to three different lawyers.”

Adrian finally couldn’t hold it back and sneered. The corners of Helena’s mouth also twitched slightly. Then, she took out a folded piece of letter paper from her handbag and spread it flat on the table.
It was handwritten.
“I tried to suppress my instinct to ‘beautify’ it,” she said in a self-deprecating tone.

Adrian recognized the warning she had borrowed from Officer Ruiz. He unfolded the paper. Helena wrote above: I thought smugly that your father’s fear made him overly cautious. I thought your mother’s fear turned her into an dangerous bomb. I thought your fear made you look incredibly naive. I even believed that my fear made me the only responsible person in this family.
How wrong I was. And the most despicable thing is that I have been making this mistake and enjoying the huge dividends brought by power. Adrian read these few lines twice.
“That’s all?” he asked.
“That’s all.”
“This is not enough to atone for your sins.”
“I know.”
He carefully folded the letter and put it into the inner pocket of his coat.
Helena looked at him. “Why did you even take it?”
“Because it’s ‘not enough atonement’, it’s still a little atonement.”
At Owen’s trial, prosecutors played the nuclear-grade video taken on the balcony. Adrian hadn’t looked at it in months.

On the court’s giant projection screen, he watched himself raise his arms in the air, pointing at Helena’s nose and yelling like a madman before Charles could finish his speech. The video quality was much blurrier than he remembered. The dazzling lights on the terrace made everyone’s faces pale and flat. The video still ends abruptly before Margot can point out the fatal mistake in the color of the paint seal.
Owen’s defense lawyer bit Adrian like a hungry wolf, asking him whether he understood what document Helena was holding.
“I don’t know.”
“Then did you know at that time that she had just taken away a tampered agreement?”
“I don’t know.”
“Have you considered solving this problem with your father privately?”
“Yes.”
“But you ultimately chose to make a public accusation in front of two hundred people.”
“Yes.”
“Because you are convinced that if confronted in private, Mrs. Ward would be able to come up with a perfect set of lies to get away with it.”
“Yes.”
“And this, your honor, is exactly what my client really thought at that time!” The defense lawyer suddenly raised his voice.
“Objection!” The prosecutor immediately jumped to his feet.
“The objection is valid.” The judge knocked down his gavel.
But these highly inflammatory words have echoed in the air of the court like a ghost.

The defense lawyer pressed forward step by step to the witness stand. “Mr. Vale, if you hadn’t stood up and made an attack in public at that time, wouldn’t it be very likely that the hugely controversial asset transfer agreement would have been completely confirmed in the subsequent engagement ceremony?”
“I don’t know.”
“It was your ground-breaking accusation that successfully prevented this disaster from happening!”
“It just interrupted the speech rudely.”
“It bravely sheds light on a governance crisis that has been brewing for a long time!”
“It only reveals a small part of it.”
The defense lawyer was choked by his uncooperative attitude and paused for a moment.
Adrian didn’t wait for him to ask any more questions and continued talking on his own. “And it makes the true truth more confusing for a long time.”
The defense lawyer frowned: “Why do you say that?”
“Because once everyone found a perfect 'villain' to blame in this farce, they felt at ease and stopped reflecting on the dirty things they had done.”
“Objection!” the prosecutor protested again.
The judge sternly warned Adrian that he was only required to answer questions and was not allowed to make lengthy personal speeches. This time, Adrian kept his mouth shut.

Owen was ultimately found guilty on all charges except the charge of “attempting to make a fraudulent transfer” due to lack of evidence. The jury believed that although the methods he used were despicable and illegal, prosecutors could not prove beyond reasonable doubt whether he wanted to take the opportunity to steal control, or whether he simply wanted to use extreme means to force an internal review.
He was sentenced to four years in federal prison. Owen was allowed to make final statements in court before the judge handed down his sentence.

He broke down in tears and said that he had watched Charles pretend to be in power over the years while ceding power to Helena without any bottom line. He insisted that he sincerely believed that if no one dared to completely pop this pustule in public, Adrian would never be able to live his own life.
Finally, he turned his head and looked straight at Adrian.
“I was not wrong about this rotten system.” He choked and said, “But I was wrong. I shouldn’t have taken advantage of you.”
Adrian knew he was telling the truth. But that doesn’t mean he can forgive him.

Six months after the engagement dinner, the probate court issued a formal ruling annulling the ridiculous transfer agreement. The judge sternly pointed out in the judgment that although Charles’s signature was confirmed to be his own, he was forced to sign it under circumstances of major concealment and asymmetric information, which did not have the legal effect of informed consent; at the same time, the sending of the electronic transfer notice was also deemed to be an unauthorized and illegal operation.
## Chapter Seventeen

Control returned to Charles with new shackles. The trust was forced to undergo a complete reorganization, replacing Helena’s monopoly with three independent trustees who had no stake in the business. Adrian also finally gained access to governance meetings that directly related to his own vested interests. Although he still does not have the right to vote.

For the first time in his life, he was allowed to step into the rooms where his fate had been decided behind his back countless times. However, the scenes in these rooms were far less treacherous than he imagined.

There are just mountains of boring spreadsheets, cold coffee, fights over pennies on insurance premiums, and long, drowsy analyzes of tax consequences. Executives interrupt each other. The experts all disagreed and became red-faced. Many times, after a whole day of meetings, not even a big decision has been made.
But Adrian felt an unprecedented sense of security amidst this messy “uncertainty.”

Charles wore the CEO shackles for another year. Finally, on an ordinary day, he announced a formal power transfer plan. The public relations release states that this decision was made after a thoughtful governance review and is fully consistent with the company’s long-term development strategy.
But in private, he had only one word to say to Adrian: He was tired.
“I used to think that leaving that place would feel like being skinned alive and cramped, and worse than death.” One evening, Charles stood on the terrace and looked at the sunset in the distance.
They were standing where the long-removed glass display table once stood.
“So how do you feel now?” Adrian asked smoothly.
“It was like being politely asked out of a party I had long since found boring.”
Adrian couldn’t help but laugh.

Charles looked across the lawn to the sparkling sea. “I hated Helena because she concocted that fatal document. I hated Owen because he pressed the detonation button. I hated Thomas because he wanted to take advantage of it like a shark that smelled blood. I even hated you because you made this family scandal known to the world.”
“You are the only one who has never blamed yourself?”
“I blame myself all the time. It’s just that putting the blame on you makes me feel less painful.”
Adrian leaned lazily against the cold stone railing.
Charles continued: “Your mother used to say that I had a terrible gift, the ability to seamlessly switch from guilt to anger before anyone in the world knew it.”
“She has really vicious eyes.”
“Yeah.”
They watched in silence as a white sailboat slid slowly on the sea level that was gradually being swallowed by the night.
After a long time, Charles suddenly said without any clue: “I should have let her go home.”
Adrian felt his throat suddenly sore.
“Which time are you talking about?” he asked with difficulty.
“That last time.”
“You thought her condition was too dangerous at the time.”
“No, I felt at that time that my own nerves had been stretched to the limit, and I simply couldn’t bear another crisis.”
“Those are two different things.”
“Indeed.”
Adrian turned his head and looked at his father steadily. Charles' eyes were still fixed on the sea, without the courage to look back.
“I selfishly took the distress signal emanating from her as a test of my personal endurance.” There was endless regret in his voice.
Adrian recalled the words Helena had written on the paper. My fear has made me the only responsible person in this family.
He didn’t pat his father on the shoulder and say, “It’s okay, it’s all over.”

Because that’s not okay at all. But he still chose to stand beside him quietly. Eleven months after returning the ring, Celia finally got it back. Not from Adrian though. Instead, I went directly to the jeweler to refund the full amount.

She and Adrian pooled that money together and put a down payment on a small apartment in Brooklyn. They didn’t give any spare keys to the apartment or the front door. They didn’t immediately rush to re-engage.
They decided to try living together first.

The water pipes in that old apartment always made a maddening noise, the kitchen was too narrow to turn around, and the damn neighbor next door had to practice playing the trumpet at ten o’clock every night. Adrian juggles his time between shipping courses at university and a two-day-a-week apprenticeship at the company. Celia resolutely quit her family’s glamorous foundation and joined a non-profit organization dedicated to improving low-income housing, earning a meager salary that would have given her mother a heart attack on the spot.
They still had heated arguments about who did the dishes, how to spend money, and whether Adrian’s surprise father should be kept out of the house.
Sometimes Adrian would fall into dead silence for hours, which he called “deep thinking.”
Celia has learned to poke holes in him mercilessly: “You may be sitting here, but your soul has fled back to your hometown.”
Sometimes, Celia would make certain decisions beforehand and only inform him lightly afterwards.
Adrian also learned to fight back: “This type of ‘protection’ with the benefit of hindsight, in my opinion, is no different from authoritarian control.”

In fact, neither of them liked this kind of heated conversation. But they still forced themselves to speak out again and again. It was a rainy Thursday two years later. That dinner seemed like it had happened in the last century. Carrying two heavy bags of groceries, Adrian pushed open the apartment door and saw Celia sitting on the kitchen floor in an embarrassed state, staring blankly at the drawer that should have been scrapped long ago.
That broken drawer finally completely derailed and died. She held a rusty screw in her hand.
“I think the load-bearing structure was completely destroyed this time,” she said seriously.
“It’s just a wooden drawer.”
“This is usually the favorite line that people who have never seen the world say before disaster strikes.”
He put the grocery bag aside.

The two of them stuck their butts out and worked together to forcefully remove the severely deformed slide rail. Behind the slide, wedged tightly in the gap between the inside of the cupboard and the wall, they unexpectedly found an old, dusty envelope that had apparently been accidentally dropped in by a previous tenant. Stuffed inside were a few greasy takeout menus, a supermarket receipt from 2009, and a photo of a group of complete strangers laughing their heads off at some birthday party.
Celia stared at the picture for a long time.
“Do you think they were really happy at that time?” she asked softly.
“At least for the second when the shutter was pressed, they seemed quite happy to take the photo.”
“You know that’s not what I asked.”
Adrian sat down next to her on the dusty linoleum floor.
“I don’t know.”

She nodded. He took out a delicate little velvet box from the gap in the grocery bag. Celia’s eyes were locked on it. Adrian had originally prepared an emotional proposal speech. He secretly rehearsed twice in front of his own reflection on the subway window, and felt nauseated each time.
He snapped open the box. Inside lay an plain platinum ring, devoid of any family gems that had been passed down for centuries.
“I don’t know how to assure you that we will never have any trouble again in our lives,” he said every word, his voice trembling slightly.
Celia’s eyes turned red.

He swallowed and continued: “I can’t guarantee that every time I encounter danger, I can trust you 100% without reservation before fear takes over my brain. But the only thing I can guarantee is that I desire... I desire that every time I mess up, I can tell you without any disguise that I failed.”
She stared at him for a long, long time.
Then, she burst into tears and laughed: “This is really the most unromantic proposal vow I have ever heard.”
“I also prepared a version before.”
“Worse than this?”
“It sucks.”
She finally couldn’t help laughing and covered her face with her hands. Adrian just waited quietly holding the box. When she lowered her hands, she stretched out her left hand directly.
“I do.” There were still tears in her eyes. “But we have to fix this damn drawer first.”

Three months later, they were married quietly at City Hall. Charles is here. Helena comes too. After two weeks of back and forth with Adrian, Celia finally decided to send her an invitation. Helena, wearing an understated dark navy dress, sat silently in the second row. When Adrian and Celia exchange vows, she sheds a silent tear. After the ceremony, she stood stiffly in the corner until Celia walked through the crowd and offered her hand.
“Thank you for coming,” Celia said.
“Thank you for letting me come.”

Helena sets her sights on Adrian. He stepped forward and gave her a hug. It was a short, stiff hug. Her body was as stiff as a stone for a moment, then slowly relaxed. There is no perfect forgiveness in this embrace.

There is only a deep understanding that transcends time and hatred. At the subsequent luncheon, Charles and Helena sat at opposite ends of the long dining table. They exchanged only one word during the entire feast - when Charles asked her, deadpan, if she could pass the salt shaker.
“Thank you, I need it,” she said.
He handed over the salt shaker. No one present was too pretentious to interpret this ordinary act as a symbol of the Great Reconciliation of the Century.

The scandal of that engagement dinner has never really been erased from people’s memories. Whenever Vale shipping makes some noise in the financial news, that old video will be dug up and re-exposed by the bad guys. People will still point behind their backs and recognize Adrian as the stupid young man who angrily pointed at the trustees on the terrace. Some praised him as a civilian hero who dared to break the black box of interests, while others called him a fool who pushed his family into the abyss. But these two extreme black and white evaluations are much easier than facing the complicated truth.

Years later, when Charles completely stepped down, Adrian did not become the sole dictatorial successor as the outside world predicted, but became one of the many directors with voting rights. One day, a new rookie analyst boldly asked him what he had learned from that chaotic night.

They were sitting in a conference room and had just finished a boring governance training. Three different versions of a proposed agreement were scattered around the large conference table, each densely marked with the date, who revised it, and the history of revisions.
Adrian looked through the transparent glass partition at the employees coming and going in the corridor outside.
“What I’ve learned is that the ‘absolute certainty’ that you believe in is usually just a first draft that someone else has carefully revised,” he said lightly.
The young analyst was eagerly waiting for him to express some business insights or philosophy of life. Adrian just smiled at him.
“That’s all.”

That evening, he drove into the old Connecticut estate. Tonight was Charles’s birthday. The once familiar terrace has long since changed. The impressive glass display table was completely moved away, and now a long wooden table is in its place. The tabletop was mottled with the marks of several circles of water glasses, and there was also a shallow scorch mark caused by the party thermos.
There was some movement in the house, where Celia was helping Charles try to get rid of the stubborn cake box.

As for Helena, she was not present and only asked someone to send a bouquet of flowers. She now teaches trust ethics in a law school clinic, specializing in providing legal aid to lower-income families who cannot afford private lawyers. Adrian now talks to her on the phone no more than twice a year. Occasionally the conversation would come back to my mother, but most of the time it was just meaningless pleasantries.
With the sound of the French double glass doors being pushed open, Charles walked out of the house. In his hand, he actually held the wireless microphone used at that disastrous dinner.
“Plucked it out of an old drawer.” He waved the thing in his hand.
Adrian’s eyes were locked on the object for a moment.
“Throw it in the trash.”
“I thought you wanted to keep a souvenir.”
“Give me a reason.”
Charles shrugged indifferently: “It’s a piece of history.”
“It’s just a loudspeaker.”
“Not entirely.”

Adrian didn’t waste any more words and grabbed the microphone directly from his hand. The bottom of the black plastic handle is already covered in scratches. He tried pressing the power switch, but nothing happened - the battery inside was dead.

afterimages of the past suddenly overlapped on the terrace: the dazzling crystal chandelier behind the glass table, the gilded envelopes scattered on the table, Helena’s hands spread out in confusion, Celia who was close to her, and Charles who froze in place in the middle of his speech. And after that shocking accusation was thrown out, all the guests looked at her in astonishment.

For a long time, he believed that it was that moment that neatly separated truth and lies into two parts. But now he suddenly realized that that moment didn’t break anything at all, it just opened the door curtain of the family’s secret room.
Adrian was silent and gently placed the abandoned microphone on the long wooden table. From inside the door, Celia’s voice called his name.
He left that piece of dead “history” on the wooden table, turned around and walked into the house.
zh: ## 第一章
突如其来的死寂让 Adrian 清晰地听见了自己的呼吸声。他能感觉到喉咙深处干涩的拉扯感，而更让他懊恼的是，Helena 显然也察觉到了他的紧绷。
“我当时去晨间休息室拿 Celia 的披肩，” 他打破了沉默，“露台的门敞开着，Helena 就站在那张展示桌前。”
“我只是在核对文件。” Helena 面不改色。
Charles 没有看她。“让他把话说完。”
Adrian 盯着她继续说道：“她手里拿着两个信封。一个是官方准备的，另一个是她自己的。我亲眼看到她从 Margot 放在桌上的那个信封里抽出了已签署的协议，然后把另一份文件塞了进去。接着，她封好了第二个信封，把它带了出来。”
Helena 微微偏了偏头。“你看到的只是纸张。”
“我看到了签名页。”
“隔着十五英尺的距离，你只是看到了某种‘看起来像’签名页的东西。”
“我看到了我父亲用蓝色墨水签下的首字母。”
Charles 的目光落在了办公桌上的信封上。
那天下午，他已经在继承协议的每一页上签了字。Adrian 对此确信无疑，因为父亲还曾满腹牢骚地抱怨过 Helena 非逼着他用的那支钢笔。
Celia 站得很近，她裸露的手臂几乎碰到了 Adrian 的衣袖。“那你为什么不立刻指出来？”
Adrian 瞥了她一眼。这个问题很尖锐，但也确实戳中了他的痛处。
“我跟着 Helena 出去了，” 他坦白道，“我想确认一下。她走进了洗手间那条走廊，回来的时候手里只剩下一个信封。紧接着，我爸就开始了致辞。”
“所以你硬生生熬过了那六分钟的致辞才发作。” Charles 的语气听不出情绪。
“因为我想，也许是我看错了。”
Helena 发出一声极轻的叹息。“你确实看错了。”
Adrian 猛地转向她：“那刚才在外面，你为什么阻止大家打开它？”
“因为当着两百位宾客的面让这个家族颜面扫地，是不可挽回的灾难。”
“狸猫换太子，偷换法律文件，同样是不可挽回的灾难！”
“Adrian。” Charles 沉声警告。
这警告的语调太熟悉了。它的潜台词是：在我处理真正重要的事情时，别逼我先来收拾你。
Adrian 闭上了嘴。
Charles 转向 Helena。“信封里到底装了什么？”
“一份修订后的执行副本。”
“谁修订的？”
“谁给你的授权？”
Helena 的嘴角抿紧了。“您。”
Charles 死死盯着她。
“不，我没有。” 他一字一顿地说。
Helena 瞥了一眼紧闭的房门，仿佛在确认这个房间的绝对私密性。“是您让我修改关于生存者设定的条款的。”
“我是让你准备几个‘备选方案’。”
“您原话说，现有的架构会让庄园面临风险。”
“我也说了，这件事我们周一再议。”
“您同样说过，订婚的消息一公布，任何拖延都是不明智的。”
“但我从未授权你进行‘替换’。”
“替换”这个词，瞬间改变了房间里的空气密度。
这不是误解。不是行政失误。不是一个神经过敏的年轻人误判了资深顾问的常规操作。
Celia 从 Adrian 身边退开一步，直视着 Helena。“你到底改了什么？”
Helena 用一种令人恼火的冷静回望她。“这目前与你无关。”
“如果我的订婚是你篡改文件的理由，那就与我有关。”
“它关乎你的未来，所以才需要被极度审慎地讨论。”
Charles 伸出手，准备去拿那个信封。
就在他触碰到的前一瞬，Helena 动了。动作不大，仅仅半步。但足够了。
Charles 的手悬停在半空。
“你往里面塞了什么？” 他厉声问。
Helena 的神情恢复了几分往日的端庄。“一份能够保护庄园免遭不必要资产转移的文件。”
“转移给谁？”
无人应答。
Adrian 感觉身旁的 Celia 浑身僵硬。
Charles 垂下视线，打量着封口。他将信封翻转过来，审视着上面凸起的皇冠浮雕。“这不是我们家的火漆印。”
“不是。” Helena 承认。
“那是谁的？”
“我的。”
Charles 抬起头。
多年来，Helena 一直在私人信笺上使用 Ward 信托合伙人的家徽，尽管那家公司早就被并入了一家大型信托机构。那顶皇冠和桂冠曾经属于她的祖父——一位纽黑文的遗嘱检验法官，他的画像至今还挂在某家法院的会议室里。
Charles 捏起了信封。
“我们现在就拆开它。”
Helena 的伪装终于裂开了一丝缝隙，透出了底层的恐惧。
“如果您在没有律师在场的情况下拆开它，可能会极大地损害您的立场。”
“什么立场？”
“在一场您甚至还没有察觉到的法律纠纷中的立场。”
Charles 毫不犹豫地撕开了封口。
声音很轻。
Adrian 原以为会看到什么极具戏剧性的东西——一份隐藏的修正案，一份伪造的转让书，或者将他扫地出门的无情条款。然而，Charles 只是抽出了一份用回形针别在顶部的十二页文件，面无表情地读着扉页。
Celia 凑近了一些。Adrian 看不清上面的字。
Charles 翻到第二页。然后是第三页。
“那到底是什么？” Adrian 忍不住问。
Charles 充耳不闻。
Helena 痛苦地闭了闭眼睛。
Charles 终于抬起头看向她。“你把 Vale 航运控股公司的投票控制权，转移到了信托基金名下。”
“我是为了保全它。”
“你把我的控股股份，划入了一个不可撤销的管理架构里。”
“信托原本就持有剩余权益。”
“那是在我死后！”
“您最近的一系列决策，已经制造了迫在眉睫的危机。”
“你是说我批准 Adrian 婚姻财产协议的决策？”
“我是说您决定将整个庄园与 Markham 家族的潜在债务捆绑在一起的决策。”
Celia 的血色瞬间从脸上褪去。“我的家族对 Vale 航运没有任何非分之想！”
“今天确实没有。” Helena 针锋相对，“但这和‘没有风险敞口’是两码事。”
Charles 将文件重重地甩在桌上。“这上面有我的签名。”
Adrian 猛地倾身向前。
在页面底部，Charles 的名字以一道坚定有力的蓝色墨迹呈现。
Charles 用食指轻轻点了一下那个签名。
“我根本没签过这份文件。”
全场落针可闻。
他又翻开另一页。蓝色的首字母缩写赫然在目，带着一点熟悉的倾斜角度。熟悉到足以封死任何质疑的嘴。
Celia 看向 Adrian。在她开口之前，他就已经读懂了她眼里的质问。
“你说你看到她替换了已签名的协议，” 她颤声问，“那你看到她签任何东西了吗？”
“没有。”
“有任何人看到吗？”
Helena 的目光飘向了他。Adrian 极其厌恶她眼神中流露出的那一抹如释重负。
Charles 拿起手机拨通了一个号码。
“Daniel，” 电话一接通他就下令，“马上来图书馆。就现在。”
他没有等对方回应就挂断了。
Daniel Price，Charles 的私人律师，今晚也带着丈夫出席了晚宴，此刻大概还在露台上假装研究一块甜点盘子。不到两分钟后，他推门而入，一看到桌上的文件，立刻关上门并扯松了领带。
## 第二章
“我听说出了点状况。” Daniel 说道。
“一份伪造了签名的控制权转移文件。” Charles 冷冷地回应。
Daniel 的眼神瞬间变得锐利起来。“所有人都别碰任何东西。”
“我已经拆开了。”
“那真是太遗憾了。”
“它当时在 Helena 手里。”
“那就更遗憾了。”
Helena 转向他：“在有人再次使用‘伪造’这个词之前，你最好先把这份执行副本和下午那套签字文件核对一下。”
Daniel 走到办公桌前，但并未触碰那些纸张。“下午的签字文件现在在哪？”
“在晨间休息室展示桌上的官方信封里。” Adrian 回答。
Daniel 立刻看向 Charles。“派人封锁那里。”
“Margot 就在门外。”
“那间屋子今晚至少有六十个人进出过。”
“是两百个。” Celia 纠正。
Daniel 掏出手机。“我让安保把南门锁上。”
Helena 双手交叠。“你正在制造一场无法收场的闹剧。”
“闹剧在你拿着一份带有未授权签名的文件走上公共仪式的台面时，就已经开始了。” Charles 反唇相讥。
她用一种近乎悲哀的眼神看着他。“您居然还在自欺欺人，认为那个签名是‘未授权’的。”
Adrian 死死盯着父亲的脸。Charles 没有退缩，但眼神深处确实闪过了一丝难以名状的波动。
“这是什么意思？” Daniel 追问。
Helena 沉默不语。
Daniel 转向 Charles。“你今天签署过任何备用草案吗？”
“没有。”
“昨天呢？”
“没有。”
“这周？”
“没有。”
“你签过空白的签名页吗？”
Charles 的沉默持续得太久了。
Adrian 猛地转头看向父亲。
Daniel 的语气变了：“Charles。”
“我周二签署了一批重组文件的确认书。”
“多少份？”
“不知道。十五份？或者二十份。”
“它们是装订在一起的吗？”
“它们是作为一整套交割文件呈递给我的。”
“谁递交的？”
Charles 看向 Helena。她毫不退让地回敬着他的目光。
Daniel 痛苦地揉了揉眉心。“你居然在没有逐一审查附件内容的情况下，就签了那一堆文件？”
“我审查了摘要。”
“Helena 准备的摘要？”
Adrian 忍不住往后退了一步，远离了那张办公桌。
图书馆里的空气似乎变得有些燥热。衬衫的领口勒得他喘不过气来。他大半辈子都认为，父亲的谨慎简直到了令人发指的地步。Charles 会反复核对餐厅的账单，在董事会后录音备份，甚至不亲自检查别人代写的生日贺卡留言就绝不签字。然而，他居然仅仅因为文件是 Helena 递上来的，就毫不犹豫地签了一整摞——只因为在过去的二十三年里，Helena 每天都在做这件事。
Celia 压低声音开口：“所以，签名可能是真的。”
“签名时，这份文件可能根本没有附在后面，” Daniel 分析道，“或者它被伪装成了其他东西混在文件包里。这是两种完全不同性质的麻烦。”
Helena 的双手依然交叠着。“这份文件就在周二的文件包里。”
Charles 瞪着她：“胡说。”
“它被列为‘或有治理文书’。”
“它当时被标明的是‘草案’！”
“目录上并没有写‘草案’。”
“但摘要里写了！”
“摘要明确指出，该文件的生效取决于某个触发事件。”
“什么触发事件？”
Helena 的目光在 Adrian 和 Celia 之间游走。
“公开订婚。”
几秒钟内，没有人说话。
Celia 突然笑了一声，毫无笑意可言。“我的订婚，触发了对他公司控制权的转移？”
“不仅仅是订婚，” Helena 解释道，“是订婚的公开宣布，再加上你家族律师提交的那份修改后的婚姻财产提案。”
“我家族的律师只发送了一份草案。”
“一份要求在未来资产增值中享有‘均等分配权’的草案。”
“那仅仅是指 Adrian 和我之间的资产。”
“除非改变现有的股权结构，否则 Adrian 未来的资产增值，与信托基金的持股是根本无法剥离的。”
Adrian 难以置信地看向 Celia。“你从来没跟我说过这个。”
“我根本不知道里面有这种条款。”
“那是你的律师写的。”
“那是‘我父亲的’律师写的！”
“但你签字认可了？”
“我只是告诉他们拟一份标准协议。”
Helena 的神情微微缓和了一点。“牵扯到家族继承控制权时，这个世界上根本不存在什么‘标准协议’。”
Charles 拎起那份转让文件。“所以你的绝妙解决方案，就是赶在订婚消息公开之前，强行夺走我的投票权？”
“我的解决方案是防止一场陷入泥潭的婚姻索赔案导致整个公司瘫痪。”
“那是‘我的’公司。”
“那是‘您家族的’公司。”
Charles 狠狠地盯着她。
Daniel 强行插入桌子和壁炉之间，用身体挡在了冲突的正中央。“今晚我们不解决条款解释的问题。现在的当务之急是封存所有文件，确认每一个版本，锁定所有人的出入权限，并且绝对不要在不必要的证人面前继续争吵。”
“我不是什么不必要的证人。” Adrian 反驳。
Daniel 看向他。“你不仅是证人，更意味着你现在必须闭嘴，直到我把你的确切口供以书面形式记录下来为止。”
Adrian 再次感受到了那种久违的屈辱——被贬低为一个只能任由他人摆布的角色。
“我很清楚我刚才看到了什么。”
“我相信你确实看到了‘一些东西’。但我现在需要知道极其精确的细节，而且是在你的记忆被接下来的十次谈话重塑之前。”
Helena 转向 Charles。“您还应该知道，这份转让文件已经设定好，将于明天上午九点送达信托基金的行政办公室。”
“是你安排的送达日程。” Daniel 戳穿她。
“你能取消吗？”
“马上取消。”
Helena 纹丝不动。
Daniel 的声音瞬间降到了冰点。“就现在。”
“这部手机操作不了。”
“那就打给能操作的人。”
“指令由外部信托顾问掌控。”
“名字。”
“Becker Lane 律所。”
Daniel 倒吸了一口凉气。“果然是他们。”
Charles 皱眉：“什么意思？”
“意思是，他们代表的是信托基金，而不是你。如果这份文件是合法的，他们的职责可能是强行推进这次转移；如果它是非法的，在弄清自身面临多大风险之前，他们依然会按兵不动。”
Charles 走到吧台车前，往水晶杯里倒了些水。直到他端起杯子的那一刻，他的手才控制不住地颤抖起来。
Adrian 看到了。Helena 也看到了。
Charles 咽下水，放下杯子，看向他的儿子。
“你站出来说话是对的。”
这句话本该带来某种救赎般的释然，然而，它却只让 Adrian 觉得自己无比稚嫩。
“你相信我？” 他问。
“我相信 Helena 在没有授权的情况下擅自挪动了文件。”
“我问的不是这个。”
Charles 的表情微微封闭了起来。“我们目前还不清楚到底发生了什么。”
Adrian 移开了视线。
Celia 想要靠近他，但他在她碰到自己之前就退开了一步。
Daniel 此刻正对着安保人员下达指令，要求他们封存晨间休息室、南走廊、图书馆和西侧服务入口的所有门禁日志。他要求拍下展示桌的现场照片，并命令任何工作人员在留下联系方式之前不得擅自离岗。
## 第三章
Helena 凝视着他，神情已近乎古井无波。
Adrian 第一个察觉到了这种变化。
“你现在不害怕了。” 他说。
她转过头。“恐慌毫无用处。”
“刚才在外面你明明很慌。”
“因为一个对前因后果一无所知的年轻人，当众指控我犯下了欺诈罪。”
“你确实掉包了信封。”
“是的。”
这声干脆的承认，让整个房间陷入了另一种诡异的安静。
Adrian 朝她走近一步。“那你为什么还要装模作样地——”
“我掉包，是因为原定要展示的那份文件，根本不是你父亲真正想要公之于众的那一份。”
Charles 放下手里的水晶杯。“把话说清楚。”
Helena 看着那只被拆开的信封。“展示桌上的那份继承协议里，把控制权转移文件作为附件悄悄塞了进去。”
Daniel 浑身一僵。“你是说官方的那份继承协议？”
“谁塞进去的？”
“我不知道。”
Charles 眯起眼睛。“你指望我们相信，你拿走了一份未授权的文件，然后又放进去了另一份未授权的文件，仅仅是为了‘保护’？”
“我用周二已经签署好的治理文书替换了那份公开的执行副本，是因为我必须在不惊动那个篡改文件的人的情况下，把那个被动手脚的文件包撤下来。”
“这简直荒谬至极。” Celia 插话道。
“如果 Helena 认为当时有人正在暗中监视那张桌子，这个逻辑就成立。” Daniel 幽幽地接口。
Adrian 震惊地看着他。“你居然在为她辩护？”
“我只是在理清逻辑，不代表我赞同她的做法。”
Charles 转向 Helena。“你为什么不直接把那个文件包交给我？”
“因为我无法确定，您是否默许了把它塞进去。”
“你大可以问我。”
“当着所有宾客的面？在您发表演讲的前几分钟？”
“你可以把我拉到一边私下说。”
“您当时正和副州长寒暄，接着是 Celia 的父母，然后又是摄影师。我必须当机立断。”
“一个极其鲁莽的决定。”
“是的。”
她回答得如此坦然，反倒让 Charles 一时语塞。
Helena 继续说道：“我原本打算在致辞结束后，把那份被篡改的协议拿给 Daniel 看。我用了自己的信封，因为我无法重新封好那个官方信封。我特意选了一份‘如果被发现，必然会引发内部审查’的文件放进去。”
Adrian 错愕地盯着她。“你是故意想被抓住的？”
“我希望这种不合理能被一个懂行的人察觉。”
“当 Margot 注意到火漆印的时候，你看起来吓坏了。”
“因为 Margot 是对着整个露台喊出来的。”
“这两者性质完全不同，” Daniel 打断了他们，“你到底为什么非要把签了字的转移文件放进你的信封里？”
“为了保持信封的重量和厚度一致。”
Daniel 的脸色又变了。“所以，任何在远处监视的人，都会误以为原本的展示文件还在原位。”
“是的。”
Charles 沉着脸说：“你的意思是，这屋里还有同谋。”
“我的意思是，桌子上的协议在我碰到它之前，就已经被人动过手脚了。”
Adrian 拼命摇头。“我亲眼看到你抽出纸张的。”
“你看到的是我拿走那份被篡改的文件包。”
“然后替换了它。”
“是的。”
“用一份带有他签名的文件。”
“是的。”
“在完全没有告知他的情况下。”
“是的。”
每一次承认，都在一点点压缩她周围的生存空间。但 Helena 一步也没有退缩。
Daniel 从桌上抽出一张干净的白纸，小心翼翼地将那份拆开的转移文件拨进一个皮革公文夹里。“我们需要找到官方的那个信封。”
一阵敲门声响起。
Margot 没等里面回应就推门而入。她的隐形耳机不见了，一缕金发从马尾里散落出来，粘在汗湿的脸颊上。
“展示信封不见了。” 她汇报道。
今晚，Charles 终于第一次彻底失去了表情管理。
“你说什么？”
“我按照吩咐锁定了晨间休息室。当请宾客们移步室内享用甜点时，信封还在桌上。但当安保关闭南门后，它就不翼而飞了。”
Daniel 猛地看向 Helena。
她纹丝未动。
Adrian 感觉到 Celia 在他身边转过了身。
Margot 喘了口气继续说：“钢笔还在。银托盘也在。唯独信封没了。”
“这段时间谁进去过？” Daniel 追问。
“大概有三分钟的时间，露台上的所有人都有可能进去。”
“监控呢？”
“Vale 先生为了保护隐私，要求关闭了露台的摄像头。”
Charles 将目光投向地面。
两年前，一张他在退休晚宴上的私人照片登上了八卦专栏，从那以后，他就立下了这个死规矩。
“室内的监控呢？” Daniel 问。
“只有走廊有。晨间休息室里没有。”
“出入口有吗？”
“立刻封锁庄园。”
Charles 猛地抬起头：“不行。”
Daniel 转身面对他：“一份极有可能被篡改过的法律文书刚刚被盗了。”
“你不能非法拘禁两百个非富即贵的宾客。”
“我可以请求他们协助调查一桩安保事故，暂时留步。”
“这会让这件丑闻在午夜前就登上新闻头条。”
“它可能已经是新闻头条了。”
仿佛是为了印证这句话，Celia 的手机震动了起来。
紧接着是 Adrian 的。
然后是 Charles 的。
Celia 第一个看清了屏幕。“有人把视频发到网上了。”
Adrian 掏出手机。
这段视频是在不到一分钟前，被一个完全陌生的账号上传的。画面里，他脸色苍白而狂怒地指着露台对面，画外音是他自己的嘶吼：她偷换了协议！
视频在 Margot 开口前戛然而止。
醒目的标题写着：【订婚晚宴惊天丑闻：Vale 家族继承人当众指控家族信托人欺诈】
Adrian 强迫自己看了两遍。
看第二遍时，他才惊觉视频里的自己有多么歇斯底里。
那不是坚毅，更不是勇敢。
那是失控的癫狂。
下方紧接着弹出了另一条推送，来自一位本地政治记者——他能收到请柬，纯粹是因为 Charles 赞助了该州一半的慈善机构。
消息人士透露：争端核心直指 Vale 航运的控制权以及一份婚姻财产协议草案。
Celia 将手机反扣在桌面上。
“我父母肯定会认为这一切都是我一手策划的。”
Adrian 错愕地看着她。“他们凭什么这么想？”
“因为 Helena 刚刚指责是我家的律师带来了隐患，而现在，一份绝密的私人协议竟然在甜点还没上桌前，就成了全网公开的八卦。”
“我没有指控你的家族。”
“但你在所有人面前指控了家族信托人。”
“因为我亲眼看到她掉包了文件！”
“而现在，那份唯一能解释她为什么这么做的文件，不见了。”
她的话里没有责备，但正因如此，才更加令人绝望。
Charles 的目光越过他们，投向图书馆紧闭的大门。门外的宾客已经不再是客人，而是一股不可控的洪流。他们此刻一定都在疯狂刷手机、给司机打电话、编造着各种版本的阴谋论。
“Margot，” 他终于妥协了，“请所有人多留十五分钟。就说庄园遗失了一份重要文件，我们需要他们的协助。”
## 第四章
“协助？” Daniel 挑眉。
“我们总不能去搜参议员的身。”
“我们可能得搜工作人员的身。”
“不行。”
“那信封可就真飞走了。”
“它可能已经飞走了。”
Daniel 死死盯着他：“你这种永远把‘面子’排在第一位的本能，正是那个房间连个监控都没有的原因！”
Charles 咬紧了牙关：“注意你的言辞。”
“不，今晚不行。”
他们几十年的交情允许了这种程度的冒犯，而这种交情里的裂痕，也毫无保留地展露在了所有人面前。
Margot 依然站在门边。“还有一个问题。”
没人接话。
“官方展示用的那个信封，封口处用的是黑色的火漆，” 她说，“不是红色的。”
Adrian 猛地看向她。
Helena 接话道：“我看到的也是黑色的。”
“但订购文具时的要求是深海军蓝。”
Charles 皱起眉头：“什么？”
Margot 走进房间。“这些信封是今早送到的。一共十二个硬质金箔信封，全部印着深海军蓝色的 Vale 家族罗盘玫瑰火漆印。五点四十的时候，我把其中一个放在了桌上。但当我六点十分再去检查时，那个印记变成黑色的了。”
“你就把它留在那儿了？” Daniel 厉声问。
“我当时以为是光线问题，让深蓝色显得更暗了。”
“还有谁知道火漆颜色的细节？”
“文具商。我的团队。内务主管 Kline 太太。Vale 先生的行政助理。还有 Helena。”
Helena 摇了摇头。“我只看过设计图，不知道最终确定的颜色。”
Margot 转向 Adrian。“你看到她拿走的那个信封，火漆是什么颜色的？”
“黑色。”
“那她留下的那个呢？”
“红色。”
“所以，那个盖着黑色火漆的信封，在 Helena 碰到它之前，就已经被人动过手脚了。”
Celia 盯着 Adrian：“那你从头到尾，有没有看到过那个印着‘深海军蓝’火漆的官方信封？”
他拼命在脑海中重构当时的画面。
晨间休息室敞开的门。搭在椅背上的披肩。站在玻璃桌前的 Helena。左右手里的金箔信封。黑色的火漆。红色的火漆。他父亲蓝色的首字母缩写。纸张摩擦的细微声响。
“没有。” 他颓然作答。
Helena 的肩膀微不可察地放松了一分。
尽管这个新线索洗清了 Helena 的部分嫌疑，但 Adrian 依然对她脸上流露出的这种释然感到一阵烦躁。
Charles 看向 Margot。“去把另外十一个信封找出来。”
“它们在上了锁的活动储藏室里。”
“去查。”
Margot 领命离去。
Daniel 将双手撑在桌面上。“我们现在面临三个棘手的问题。第一：Charles 究竟有没有在知情的情况下签署那份转移文件。第二：是谁把篡改过的协议塞进了黑色信封里。第三：在刚才那场指控发生后，又是谁把信封从桌上偷走了。”
“还有第四个，” Celia 补充道，“是谁在所有人都还没离开露台之前，就把视频发到了网上。”
Daniel 看了她一眼。“对。”
Adrian 死死盯着自己的手机屏幕。最初的那个帖子已经被大V号疯狂转发。底下的评论区里挤满了昨天还不知道他是谁，今晚却已经化身微表情专家和心理学大师的网民。
特权富二代在订婚宴上精神崩溃。
信托基金小王子惊醒，发现家产要没。
这女的还不快跑等什么呢。
他按灭了屏幕。
Helena 一直在注视着他。
“这就是我拼尽全力想要避免的局面。” 她说。
Adrian 迎上她的目光。“而你当时手里正捏着一份绝密的资产转移文件。”
“所以你在连它到底是什么都没搞清楚之前，就把它彻底曝光了。”
“你本可以停下来，好好解释清楚的。”
“如果我解释，你会听吗？”
他张了张嘴，却什么也没说出来。
Celia 双臂抱胸。“我倒是很想知道，为什么这份控制权转移文件，一开始会和我们的订婚扯上关系？”
Charles 示意 Daniel：“现在不是讨论这个的时候。”
“就是现在！” 她提高了音量，“我的名字已经被卷进这个泥潭里了。”
“转让文件里没有你的名字。”
“但我的家族被当成了某种债务隐患来防范！”
“那是 Helena 擅作主张。”
“但她的借口是我们家律师发来的草案。”
Charles 的沉默，比任何否认都更让 Celia 抓狂。
她深吸了一口气，转向 Adrian。“你仔细看过那份婚姻财产草案吗？”
他心虚地看着她。
为了这份协议，他们已经推诿敷衍了整整三个星期。当双方律师在条款上唇枪舌剑时，他们俩却在为婚礼日期、宾客名单，以及婚后是翻新港口旁边的小别墅还是搬去曼哈顿这种事争论不休。每次提到协议，Celia 就会推说交给她父亲的律师处理；每次 Adrian 的律师打来电话，他都任由留言信箱吃灰，第二天再说。
“我看了摘要。” 他硬着头皮回答。
她嘴角扯出一个苦涩的弧度。“你当然只看摘要。”
Charles 复杂的目光投向儿子。他们父子间在此刻展现出的惊人相似性，显得如此讽刺。
Adrian 也意识到了这一点。
Daniel 的手机响了。他扫了一眼屏幕，接通电话。
“我是 Price。”
他听着那头的汇报。
“什么时候的事？”
他的视线像刀片一样扫向 Helena。
“把记录发给我。”
他挂断电话。
“怎么了？” Charles 问。
“Becker Lane 律所在今晚六点三十二分，收到了一份电子转移通知。”
Helena 看了一眼壁炉上的挂钟。
露台上的当众指控，发生在七点十八分。
Daniel 继续说道：“通知里附带着那份已签署的治理文书的扫描件，并指示原件将于明天送达。”
“谁发的？” Charles 的声音冷得像冰。
“发送端使用的是 Helena 公司的加密凭证。”
所有人的目光齐刷刷地刺向了她。
Helena 没有辩解。
Daniel 摊开手。“手机。”
她盯着他。
“现在，马上。”
Helena 从晚宴包里掏出一部纤薄的黑色手机，放在了办公桌上。
“密码。”
“不行。”
Charles 低声唤了她的名字，带着警告。
“我的手机里装满了涉及其他客户的特权通讯记录。”
Daniel 发出一声毫无温度的冷笑。“你现在跟我谈保密特权？”
“我现在是在避免进一步违背职业操守，因为这屋子里的每个人都已经乱了阵脚！”
“你的凭证发送了一份极具争议的控制权转移文件！”
“那不代表是我发的！”
“那就把手机解锁！”
“我会把它交给独立的第三方律师审查。”
“你必须把它交给我！”
“你代表不了 Charles。”
Daniel 猛地直起身子。“二十年来，你只要觉得对自己有利，就一直把自己当成他唯一的代言人！”
Helena 的脸色瞬间铁青。“而你二十年来，一直靠着给他提供那些他根本不听的建议来开天价账单！”
Charles 带着一种属于迟暮之年的疲倦，强行介入了他们之间。那一瞬间，他看起来远不止五十二岁。“都给我闭嘴。”
第二次敲门声响起。
Margot 抱着一个白色的储物纸箱走了进来。
她把箱子放在边桌上，掀开盖子。里面整整齐齐地码放着十一个金箔信封，每个都封着印有 Vale 家族罗盘玫瑰的深海军蓝火漆。
“多余的都在这儿了，一个不少。” 她说，“但是，我在防潮油纸下面，发现了这个。”
她捏起一条细长的黑色火漆残片。
在 Margot 放下它之前，Daniel 迅速拍了张照片。
“这是从某个封口上掉下来的？” 他问。
## 第五章
“是封口边缘脱落的残渣，上面还粘着一丝金箔纸的纤维。” Margot 答道。
“这意味着，有人拆开了其中一个深海军蓝信封，然后用黑色的火漆重新封上了它。” Celia 敏锐地指出。
Margot 点点头。
“这有可能是在储藏室里干的吗？”
“纸箱在四点半就被锁起来了。钥匙一直在我这儿，直到五点十五分，内务主管 Kline 太太借走去清点文具数量。”
Charles 猛地看向房门。“Kline 太太现在在哪？”
Margot 犹豫了一下。
“她十分钟前离开了。”
Daniel 的眼神瞬间变得可怕起来。“在庄园被封锁之前？”
“她说她丈夫突然胸口疼。”
“有人核实过吗？”
“没有。”
Charles 痛苦地闭上了眼睛。
Kline 太太掌管 Vale 庄园的内务已经整整十一年了。她负责安排维修，监督家庭账目，甚至清楚地知道哪扇门在冬天会发涩卡住。Adrian 还记得，他十五岁那年生病，门外总是莫名其妙地多出几块姜糖，而她总是装作不知道是谁放的。
Helena 从壁炉旁发话：“给她打电话。”
Margot 拨了号码。
电话响了六声，直接转入了语音信箱。
她又试了一次。
还是无人接听。
Daniel 咬牙道：“我们必须报警。”
Charles 猛地盯着他：“以什么名义？”
“盗窃。”
“盗窃一个我们甚至无法证明里面到底装了什么的破信封？！”
“我们有 Margot 提供的监管链条，Adrian 的目击证词，火漆残渣，网上的爆料视频，还有一份通过被盗用凭证发送的电子转移通知。”
“报警吧。” Celia 突然开口。
Charles 看向她。
“这件事已经满城风雨了。” 她平静地继续，“试图把它捂在家里解决，已经是不可能的事了。”
他的目光缓缓移向 Adrian。
不需要任何言语，Adrian 就能读懂父亲眼里的挣扎。这到底还是不是我们的家务事？我们还能不能把它控制在可控的范围内？
他想起了 Kline 太太偷偷留下的姜糖。
他想起了站在展示桌前的 Helena。
他想起了自己在两百名宾客面前，高高举起的那只手臂。
“我不知道。” Adrian 疲惫地说。
Charles 脸上的失望之情还没来得及掩饰，就彻底暴露了。
这激起了 Adrian 的逆反心理。“你到底想让我说什么？说这一切都是 Helena 干的？可现在看来可能真不是她。说 Kline 太太是个贼？也许她丈夫真的病危了！我只看到了冰山一角，却偏偏把它当成了绝对的真理来宣判。”
“但你看到的那一小部分，足够让你强行中止这场晚宴。” Celia 冷冷地说。
“却不足以让我搞清楚背后的原因。”
Helena 用一种让人捉摸不透的眼神注视着他。
Daniel 拨通了当地警察局长的私人号码。
十八分钟后，第一批警员从服务通道秘密进入庄园。此时，宾客们已经被允许离开，前提是留下姓名，并承诺保留在致辞期间拍摄的任何照片或视频。大多数人端着被冒犯的尊严配合了调查。少数人骂骂咧咧地要求给个说法。一位主要捐赠人的妻子甚至冷嘲热讽地问，这场订婚到底还算不算数，仿佛她购买的某种高收益债券突然暴雷了似的。
Adrian 留在图书馆里做笔录。
负责问询的女警官名叫 Ruiz，态度公事公办，不带一丝敬畏。她要求他极其精确地描述当时的距离、角度、光线、时间点，甚至具体到哪只手拿着哪个信封。当 Adrian 在描述中使用“替换”这个词时，她毫不客气地打断了他。
“描述动作本身，” 她要求道，“不要加上你自己的主观结论。”
他只能尽力还原。
Helena 的左手拿着那个盖有黑色火漆的金箔信封。她用右手抽出了一叠文件。她把文件平放在玻璃桌上。她打开了那个带红色火漆的信封——虽然此时它可能还没封口，Adrian 在心里默默纠正自己。她把另一叠完全不同的文件塞了进去。接着，她拿起桌上的那叠文件，塞进了那个黑色火漆的信封里。
“她把那个黑色的信封留在桌上了吗？” Ruiz 问。
“没有，她拿着它朝走廊走去。”
“然后带着那个红色的回来了？”
“你看到那个黑色的信封被藏去哪儿了吗？”
“没有。”
“你当时在走廊里还看到其他人了吗？”
Adrian 闭上眼睛拼命回忆。
一个端着折叠餐巾的侍者走了过去。一个男人站在洗手间门口低头看手机。一个穿着米色西装的人穿过大厅，走向西侧走廊。
“我记不清了。”
“没关系。不要试图‘美化’或者‘补全’你的记忆。”
这句话像一根刺一样扎进了他的心里。
不要试图美化它。
Adrian 这一生中，有太多事情都是在事后被“美化”过的。他母亲从来不是“抛弃”了家庭，她只是“去寻求治疗”了。他被寄宿学校开除，被公关成了“自愿休学”。Charles 和妹妹长达两年的决裂，被粉饰成了“地理位置上的疏远”。Vale 家族从不赤裸裸地撒谎，他们只是精心地打磨每一件事，直到没有任何棱角会划伤家族的光鲜招牌。
Ruiz 警官继续问：“是什么让你决定当众指控她？”
“我以为我父亲马上就要承认那份被调包的假文件了。”
“你完全可以私下提醒他，不是吗？”
“那你为什么不这么做？”
Adrian 将目光投向窗外。
草坪上，工作人员正在将露台上的蜡烛一根一根地熄灭。
“因为我觉得，如果我私下说，她绝对有办法把这事糊弄过去。”
“她以前这么做过吗？”
他瞥了一眼远处的 Helena。
她此刻正站在房间的另一端配合另一名警官的问询，她的手机已经被装进了证物袋——这是独立律师讨价还价后达成的临时妥协。
“做过。” Adrian 回答。
Helena 若有所感地看了过来。
Ruiz 顺着他的目光看去，但并未追问细节。
做完笔录后，Adrian 在昏暗厨房旁边的早餐室里找到了 Celia。她摘下了耳环，随意地扔在桌上的一碗柠檬旁边。她的父母没有向 Charles 辞行就径直离开了。她母亲发来信息，问是否需要家里的司机折返回来接她。
Adrian 站在门口。
“你要走吗？” 他问。
“我不知道。”
他拉开她对面的椅子。
她看着他：“求你了，别用那种好像我们接下来要讨论怎么布置鲜花一样的姿态坐下来。”
他顿住了，保持着站立的姿势。
冰箱的压缩机发出嗡嗡的启动声。厨房某处的制冰机里传来冰块翻滚的闷响。
Celia 揉着耳垂上被耳环压出的红印。“我父亲说，那份婚姻财产草案里，根本没有提到要染指 Vale 航运的控制权。”
“但 Helena 说，草案里要求在未来的资产增值中享有均等分配权。”
“是的。那是针对婚内取得的资产。”
“但我信托里的分红，是可以被用来购买那些‘婚内取得’的资产的。”
“那和直接索要公司的股权根本不是一回事。”
“我知道。”
“你真的知道吗？”
她的声音很轻，却字字诛心。
Adrian 低头看着自己擦得锃亮的皮鞋，右脚的鞋尖上沾了一抹露台上的灰尘。
## 第六章
“我没有通读整份草案。” 他承认。
“我知道。”
“我本该看的。”
“是啊。”
他等着她继续质问，但她没有。
“我在逃避，” 他艰难地剖析自己，“每一次律师发来修改意见，我都觉得……我们似乎正在把未来的婚姻，翻译成各种可能会互相伤害的条款。”
“这正是法律协议的意义所在。在人们真正互相伤害之前，把潜在的伤害明码标价。”
“我讨厌这种感觉。”
“我也一样。”
“但你表现得好像这根本不是什么大事。”
“因为如果我表现出哪怕一点点的抵触，我父亲就会立刻指责我不知道保护自己。”
Adrian 终于还是拉开椅子坐了下来。不因为鲜花，仅仅是因为他站得腿酸了。
Celia 在指尖把玩着那枚耳环。“你是不是觉得，我的家人贪图你的钱？”
“没有。”
她静静地等着。
“……偶尔会有这种念头。” 他挫败地承认。
她的表情变了。不是勃然大怒，而是嘴角一直紧绷着的某种东西，彻底垮掉了。
“为什么？”
“因为这屋子里的每个人都在盘算这些。”
“我问的是，你为什么会这么想？”
他看向黑漆漆的窗户，玻璃上倒映着他们漂浮在草坪上空的影子。
“你父亲总是把信托的架构说成是‘中世纪的残余’。”
“他连他常去的俱乐部里的停车规定都骂作中世纪的残余。”
“他还总是有意无意地试探，问我以后能不能直接掌权。”
“他那是担心你一辈子都掌不了权！”
“他凭什么操心这个？”
“凭我要嫁给你啊！”
Adrian 猛地转回视线看着她。
Celia 将耳环重重地搁在桌面上。“只要有人问起你父亲是不是掌控了你的人生，你脑子里听到的第一反应永远是‘贪婪’。”
“你这么说不公平。”
“是啊，确实不公平。”
“我当众指控 Helena，仅仅是因为当时拿着那个信封的人是她！”
“更是因为这些年来，你一直迫切地想找一个替罪羊，把所有的怨气都撒在她身上。”
他猛地站起身。
Celia 的眼眶红了，但硬是没有让眼泪掉下来。“看吧，就是这样。只要有人戳破了你心知肚明的真相，你转身就逃。”
“我今晚刚刚当众指控了一个女人犯下欺诈罪，我现在不需要你来给我做心理诊断。”
“我不是在给你做诊断。我只是在告诉你，我为什么会感到害怕。”
他在门口停下了脚步。
她继续说道：“不是因为钱。而是因为，你可以隐忍几个月，把所有疑虑憋在心里，然后突然在毫无征兆的情况下，做出某种不可挽回的毁灭性举动。”
这句话比网上的那些恶毒评论还要锋利，比 Charles 的怀疑还要致命。
Adrian 转过身：“她确实掉包了协议。”
“我知道。”
“我没有错。”
“你没有‘全错’。”
“你现在的语气听起来简直像极了 Helena。”
“也许 Helena 也并不是什么事都做错了。”
他难以置信地瞪着她。
Celia 紧紧咬住嘴唇。“我不是那个意思——”
“你就是那个意思。”
“我的意思是，人性是复杂的，人们做出可怕的事情，背后的原因往往没那么简单。”
“所以这就值得原谅了？”
“那你到底想说什么？”
“我想说，我不知道我能不能嫁进这样一个家庭——在这里，每一次分歧都会升级为对忠诚的审判，每一张法律文书的背后都藏着致命的陷阱。”
Adrian 觉得整个房间的空气都在剧烈收缩。
“你是要解除婚约吗？”
“我只是请求给我一个晚上，让我不用被逼着立刻做出决定。”
他看向她左手上的订婚戒指。
她顺着他的目光看去，然后用右手捂住了它。
“这不是回答。” 他说。
“这是我目前唯一能给出的诚实回答。”
在她看到他眼底深藏的痛苦之前，他逃离了房间。
到了午夜时分，庄园已经空荡荡的，只剩下警察、律师、几名核心佣人，以及四个在几个小时前还自以为彼此之间知根知底的人。
警方在诺沃克医院找到了 Kline 太太。她的丈夫确实在傍晚六点五十八分突发了心脏问题。医院的监控和停车记录证实，她在七点二十左右抵达，也就是 Adrian 发出指控的前后。她绝对不可能在指控发生后，溜回休息室偷走信封。
但她承认，自己在五点十五分的时候拆开了那个存放文具的纸箱。
她也承认，当时她就发现少了一个深海军蓝印记的信封。
但她没有上报。
当 Ruiz 警官问及原因时，Kline 太太说她以为 Margot 已经提前拿走去布置露台了。而 Margot 坚称她是在五点四十才去拿的。
这个时间差，留下了整整二十五分钟的空白。
安保监控显示，在这段时间里，Helena 进过两次晨间休息室，Margot 进了三次，Kline 太太一次，Charles 的行政助理两次，还有两名花艺师，一名灯光师，三名侍者，以及——Celia 的父亲，Thomas Markham。
Thomas 是在五点二十七分独自走进去的，在里面逗留了整整四分钟。
Celia 在图书馆里盯着监控画面。
“我父亲当时在找 Charles。” 她极力辩解。
站在 Daniel 椅子后面的 Charles 冷笑了一声：“在晨间休息室里找？”
“他根本不知道大家都在哪儿。”
“他在这座庄园里参加了十二年的活动。”
“那他也有可能走错路！”
视频里，Thomas 从房间退出来的瞬间，Daniel 按下了暂停键。他两手空空。
Helena 倾身凑近屏幕。“倒回去一点。”
Daniel 倒退了几秒。
Thomas 进去的时候，西装外套的扣子是扣好的。出来的时候，扣子解开了。
“这根本证明不了什么。” Celia 咬牙道。
“确实，” Helena 附和了一句，“证明不了。”
Adrian 站在书架旁。自从在早餐室那场争执后，他就再也没跟 Celia 讲过一句话。她手上的戒指还在。
Ruiz 警官询问是否可以请 Thomas 配合做个笔录。Celia 拨通了他的电话。
他秒接。
“他们到底在拿你怎么样？” 他的声音大得连 Adrian 都能听见。
“爸，晚宴开始前，你为什么去了晨间休息室？”
死寂。
“我在找 Charles。”
“找他干什么？”
“想私下跟他谈谈。”
“谈什么？”
又是一阵沉默。
“关于协议的事。”
图书馆里的每一个人都瞬间竖起了耳朵。
Celia 闭上眼睛。“关于协议的什么事？”
“我想让他知道，我对此有一些顾虑。”
“什么顾虑？”
“电话里说不清楚。”
“警察就在这里。”
“那就等我过去，光明正大地跟他们谈。”
“你碰过那个金箔信封吗？”
“绝对没有。”
“你看到它了吗？”
“我看到桌上有个信封。”
“火漆是什么颜色的？”
“不知道。反正是深色。”
“你打开过它吗？”
“绝无可能。”
“那你离开房间的时候，为什么把西装外套的扣子解开了？”
Thomas 那头的沉默突然变得锋利起来。
“谁告诉你的？”
“有监控。”
“我觉得热。”
“当时的室温是华氏63度（约17摄氏度）。”
“我之前喝了酒。”
“在下午五点二十七分？”
“Celia。” 他加重了语气。
她握紧了手机：“你到底有没有从那个房间里带走任何东西？”
“没有。”
“那你有没有把任何东西放进去？”
“没有。”
Ruiz 警官伸出手，示意要把手机接过去。
Celia 妥协了。
“Markham 先生，我是达里恩警察局的 Ruiz 警官。我想请您回到 Vale 庄园，配合我们的调查。”
## 第七章
Thomas 在电话那头回了一句，但 Adrian 听不清内容。
Ruiz 面不改色。“您目前没有被逮捕。您也有权要求律师在场。”
她静静地听着。
“最好是今晚。”
又是一阵沉默。
“我明白了。”
她挂断电话。
“他正带着律师赶过来。”
Celia 转过身去，不看任何人。
Adrian 想要走向她，但双腿像灌了铅一样无法动弹。
四十分钟后，Thomas 到了，换了一辆车。他的律师，一位穿着灰色大衣、干练刻薄的女人率先发难，强烈抗议在图书馆进行审讯。Ruiz 警官将他们带到了餐厅。
闲杂人等一律被拒之门外。
Charles 吩咐人给留守的工作人员送了些咖啡。Margot 站在走廊里，一边喝着咖啡，一边在一块平板电脑上核对清单。Helena 拒绝了任何饮品。Daniel 捏着小半个放在带盖篮子里的餐包慢慢啃着，似乎连他自己都不知道这面包是怎么跑到他手里的。
Adrian 上楼换衣服。
他的卧室被打理得井井有条，仿佛他依然是这个家里的座上宾。床头备着清水，床铺已经铺好，旁边还放着一张印着早餐供应时间的精美卡片。梳妆台上摆着一张他十七岁时的照片，那是在他母亲去世前的那个夏天拍的。照片里的他正看着镜头外什么好笑的事情放肆大笑，而 Charles 站在他身旁，手搭在他的肩膀上，目光没有看镜头，而是温柔地注视着他。
Adrian 扯下领结，随手扔在地毯上。
他的手机里躺着 31 个未接来电和两百多条未读信息。两个大学同学发来八卦，问 Helena 是不是正在图谋他的继承权。一个他在大学里谈过三个月短命恋爱的女孩发来一句“你还好吗？”，过了五分钟又补了一句“我早就知道你们家骨子里透着不正常”。
他再次点开了那段视频。
他看着自己高高举起的手臂。
他清晰地记起了那前一秒的心理活动：Charles 正在台上慷慨陈词，说 Vale 家族的传承不仅依靠管理，更仰仗于“信任”。Helena 从他的余光中闪过。她手里刺眼的红色火漆。以及那种几乎要将他吞噬的确定感——如果他不立刻站出来，某种极其可怕且不可逆转的事情就会发生。
但其实，当时还有另一种隐秘的情绪。
一种病态的释然。
在那纯粹而爆裂的一秒钟里，把手指指向 Helena，卸下了他内心深处积压多年的所有猜忌。她是潜在的威胁。而他是唯一的目击者。这一次，他的父亲终于不得不顺着他手指的方向去正视现实。
他瘫坐在床沿，双手痛苦地捂住了脸。
敞开的房门被敲响了。
Charles 站在走廊里，脱掉了西装外套，只穿着那件午夜蓝的马甲，这让他看起来透着一种罕见的疲态。
“Thomas 已经承认是他拿走了原本的信封。” 他开口道。
Adrian 放下双手。
“为什么？”
“他说，他打开信封是为了检查 Helena 有没有把那份转移文件塞进去。”
“这根本说不通。”
“确实说不通。”
“那他看到了什么？”
“一份正常的继承协议，后面附带着那份资产转移文件。”
“所以 Helena 刚才说的是实话。”
“至少在这个细节上，是实话。”
“那信封现在在哪儿？”
“Thomas 坚称他看后就把它原封不动地放回了桌上。”
“那后来是谁拿走的？”
“他不知道。”
Adrian 站起身。“他篡改了里面的文件吗？”
“他矢口否认。”
“你相信他吗？”
Charles 的目光落在了梳妆台上的那张旧照片上。
“我相信 Thomas 是在为他女儿的未来感到恐惧。”
“你这不算回答。”
“这确实不算。” Charles 淡淡地说。
Adrian 等着。
父亲走进房间，弯腰捡起地毯上的领结。他带着一丝熟练得让人心酸的无奈，将它平整地放在梳妆台上。Adrian 差点被这个充满生活气息的细微动作逗笑。
“你母亲生前最恨这种虚伪的晚宴。” Charles 缓缓说道。
Adrian 诧异地看着他。
“她常常在晚宴进行到一半的时候就不见人影。后来我发现，她总是躲在洗衣房里跟那些外烩服务生聊天。她说那些底层人是这座房子里唯一会说真话的人。”
“但你从来不允许她这么做。”
“我阻止不了她。”
“但你一直试图约束她。”
Charles 摩挲着梳妆台的边缘。“是的。”
他们父子俩就这么静静地站在房间里，隔着那张记录了短暂美好时光的旧照片。
Adrian 打破了沉默：“你为什么那么信任 Helena，信任到甚至连看都不看一眼就签下她递过来的文件？”
“因为在我父亲中风倒下后，是她一手力挽狂澜，保住了这家公司没有被分拆。因为她敏锐地嗅到了别人根本没发现的税务黑洞。因为她强硬地阻止了你叔叔把他的剩余权益变卖给一家企图肢解信托的秃鹫基金。因为，当你母亲病重的时候……Helena 处理了那些我根本没有勇气去面对的事情。”
“她帮着你，把妈妈彻底从这个家里排挤了出去。”
Charles 的面部肌肉剧烈地抽搐了一下。
“她建议我，必须保护你。”
“保护我免受她的伤害？”
“免受那种情绪极度不稳定的伤害。”
“妈妈只是病了！”
“是的。”
“但你当时的反应，就像是她犯了什么不可饶恕的道德重罪。”
“我把她的病当成了一种极其危险的威胁，因为我当时也快被恐惧压垮了。”
Adrian 难以置信地瞪着他。
Charles 极少承认自己也会害怕。在父亲的字典里，只存在“顾虑”、“风险敞口”、“不利因素”。“恐惧”这种怯懦的词汇，只属于那些软弱的普通人。
“她曾经求着想回家。” Adrian 咬着牙说。
“她回来过两次。”
“然后你又把她狠心送走了。”
“因为她拒绝按时吃药。”
“她说过，那些药让她觉得自己像一具行尸走肉！”
“然后她就在雨夜里，喝得烂醉，开着车载着你在高速上狂飙。”
Adrian 移开了视线。
雨点砸在挡风玻璃上的声音。母亲那夸张得有些瘆人的笑声。凌晨两点，Charles 脸色铁青地出现在警察局。Helena 蹲在他面前，用极其温柔的语气问他有没有撞到头。
这些年，他的记忆被强行割裂成了两个极端阵营。母亲的温柔和脆弱占据了一边，而她的破坏力和危险占据了另一边。Charles 和 Helena 以一种不容置疑的强势姿态全盘接管了第二个阵营，以至于时间久了，Adrian 甚至忘记了去思考——在那张坚不可摧的面具下，他们是否也曾经和他一样恐惧无助过。
Charles 深吸了一口气：“Helena 也不是永远都是错的。”
“但这并不能洗白她今晚的所作所为。”
“当然不能。”
“你觉得那份转移文件是她伪造的吗？”
“我认为，是她亲手构建了一个权力极度膨胀的系统，一个允许她在不请示我的情况下就能先斩后奏的系统。因为在过去，我总是奖励她的这种‘超前预判’。”
Adrian 盯着他看。
Charles 继续说道：“我也认为，今晚有另一只黑手，利用了她构建的这个系统。”
“Thomas？”
“有可能。”
“那 Celia 呢？”
Charles 的眼神瞬间变得凌厉：“不可能。”
“你回答得太快了。”
“因为她没有理由去精心策划一场企业控制权的转让，来亲手毁掉自己的订婚宴。”
“但她可能早就知道草案里有针对家族财产的苛刻条款。”
“这和亲自动手篡改文件是两码事。”
Adrian 颓然坐回床沿。
Charles 依然站着，居高临下地看着他。
“你今晚当众把 Helena 的尊严踩在了脚下。” 他突然发难。
## 第八章
Adrian 猛地抬起头。“是她先偷换了文件。”
“是的。”
“她还刻意隐瞒！”
“是的。”
“当我对质时，她还在撒谎狡辩！”
“因为她在还没搞清楚你到底掌握了多少底牌之前，本能地想要自保。”
“你每次都是这样。”
“什么？”
“把那个做出恶劣行径的人，洗脑成被逼无奈的受害者，而把揭露问题的人说成是麻烦制造者。”
Charles 的表情冷了下来。“就算你的怀疑是百分之百正当的，你的‘行为方式’依然会引发灾难性的后果。”
“所以我就该像个傻子一样闭嘴？”
“我没这么说。”
“但你刚才说我羞辱了她。”
“你确实羞辱了她。”
“她可能早就暗中架空了你的公司！”
“她也可能刚刚拼尽全力，阻止了另一个人把你的公司洗劫一空！”
Adrian 猛地从床上弹了起来。“你来这儿，就是为了教训我做错了吗？！”
“我来这儿是为了告诉你，仅仅因为你在某个细节上占了理，并不意味着你可以用这种杀敌八百自损一千的方式去伸张正义。这种破坏力，是无法被抹平的。”
Adrian 觉得胸膛里像塞了一把碎玻璃。
“滚出去。”
Charles 纹丝未动。
“我叫你滚出去！”
父亲静静地看了他几秒钟，然后极轻地点了一下头，转身走出了房间。
凌晨三点，警方终于找到了那个丢失的信封。
它被丢弃在女宾衣帽间的一个华丽的金属废纸篓里，上面还盖着一堆揉皱的纸巾和两张废弃的座位卡。黑色的火漆印已经被彻底破坏。金箔纸的一角有明显的折痕。
而里面的文件，不翼而飞。
是一名在清理宾客遗留物品的工作人员发现的。
这个地点立刻引出了一长串的嫌疑人名单。今晚几乎每一位女宾客都进去补过妆。几位男宾客也曾在门口徘徊。工作人员更是频繁进出。
但走廊的高清摄像头清晰地记录下，Helena 在七点十二分走进去，七点十四分走出来。那正是在 Adrian 当众发难的四分钟前。
Helena 看着监控录像，一言不发。
Ruiz 警官冷峻地问她进去干什么。
“去藏那个盖着黑色火漆的信封。”
Adrian 震惊地盯着她。
她继续供述：“我把那份被篡改过的协议从晨间休息室拿出来，塞进了黑色信封里。我不想在还没来得及和 Daniel 沟通之前，被人当场从我身上搜出这颗定时炸弹。”
“所以你就把它当垃圾扔了？” Ruiz 满脸写着不可理喻。
“我是把它‘暂时’藏匿起来。”
“藏在一个公共衣帽间里？”
“藏在一个套着垃圾袋的废纸篓底部。那种高级场合，在晚宴结束前是绝不会有人去倒垃圾的。”
“但你失算了。”
“是的。”
“你把它扔进去的时候，里面装的是什么文件？”
“那份被篡改的继承协议。”
“里面包含那份备受争议的控制权转移文件吗？”
“是的。”
“有谁知道你把它藏在那儿了？”
“没有别人。”
